LAMATA to deploy 24 new coaches to boost red line Services
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority (LAMATA) has announced plans to strengthen operations on the Lagos Rail Mass Transit Red Line with the deployment of three new train sets comprising 24 coaches. The Managing Director of LAMATA, Mrs. Abimbola Akinajo, disclosed this while responding to service challenges and complaints by passengers using the Red Line. Akinajo acknowledged the inconvenience caused by occasional service disruptions and operational limitations, assuring commuters that the authority was working to improve service delivery, operational efficiency and customer satisfaction. According to her, the additional train sets are expected to increase the operational capacity of the Red Line, improve service frequency and accommodate more passengers. She said LAMATA was working with its technical and operational partners to ensure the trains were deployed as quickly as practicable while addressing existing challenges across the rail network. Akinajo appealed to commuters to remain patient, acknowledging their concerns and appreciating those who had continued to use the service despite the disruptions. She reiterated the authority’s commitment to improving the reliability and quality of rail transportation in Lagos. items.title: Iran's flogging of singer was warning from anxious hardliners, insiders say
items.description: By Parisa Hafezi, Emily Giles and Melory Ghazi DUBAI, Nov 28 (Reuters) - Iran's flogging of a female singer this week for offending public decency was a display of force by an embattled clerical elite straining to uphold public obedience it once took for granted, Iranian insiders say. Parastoo Ahmadi, 29, and four members of her production team received 74 lashes each on Monday for a livestreamed performance in a caravanserai near the holy Shi'ite Muslim city of Qom in which she had bare shoulders, no headscarf and male musicians, defying Iran's theocratic legal code.

items.title: 2027 Polls: INEC begins nationwide mock accreditation, 490 units in Lagos
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is conducting a six-hour nationwide mock voter accreditation exercise today, Saturday, as part of preparations for the 2027 general elections. The exercise, scheduled to run from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., is designed to assess the operational readiness of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), test the real-time transmission of results to the INEC Result Viewing (IReV) portal and identify possible technical and logistical challenges ahead of the main elections. INEC clarified that the exercise is not an actual election but a test run to ensure the efficiency of its electoral technologies ahead of the presidential and National Assembly elections scheduled for January 16, 2027. Nationwide, the exercise is taking place in 17,676 polling units, comprising two selected polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas. Only registered voters whose polling units have been selected for the exercise are expected to participate. 490 polling units in Lagos In Lagos State, 490 polling units will participate in the exercise, representing two polling units in each of the 245 registration areas across the state’s 20 local government areas. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Lagos State, Prof. Ayobami Salami, said the comprehensive list of selected polling units had been displayed at all INEC local government offices to enable residents to confirm their locations. Meanwhile, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has cancelled the November monthly environmental sanitation exercise, which was originally scheduled for today, to ensure unrestricted movement and encourage residents’ participation in the mock accreditation exercise. In Lagos Central Senatorial District, approximately 148 polling units across five local government areas have been selected for the exercise. The breakdown shows that Surulere Local Government Area has 46 polling units across 23 wards, including Aguda, Ijeshatedo, Itire, Ikate, Orile and Coker. Lagos Island has 40 polling units across 20 wards, including Araromi Odo, Epetedo, Idumagbo, Lafiaji, Olosun, Eiyekole and Okepopo. Lagos Mainland has 22 polling units across 11 wards, covering areas such as Ebute Metta, Glover, Alagomeji, Oyingbo, Iwaya and Yaba. Apapa has 20 polling units across 10 wards, including Apapa I–IV and Iganmu, while Eti-Osa also has 20 polling units across 10 wards, covering Ikoyi-Obalende, Victoria Island I and II, Ikoyi I and II, Iru/Victoria Island, Ilasan, Ajah, Sangotedo and Awoyaya. INEC urged eligible voters in the selected polling units to participate in the exercise within the six-hour window to familiarise themselves with the accreditation technology and help ensure a seamless voting process during the 2027 elections. However, as of 7:30 a.m. on Saturday, no activity had been recorded at the selected polling units, as voters were yet to arrive for the exercise. Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
items.description: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said Saturday an Israeli strike killed two staff members at a clinic in Gaza, with the Israeli army alleging that the pair were members of Hamas. The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) claimed the men, who worked as security guards at the clinic, were Hamas artillery cell commander Moaz Yousef Alitsbach and Ahmed Sufyan Muhammad Ali Abu. MSF said it was “devastated” by the killings and denounced “a direct hit” on the organisation. “Our premises were clearly marked with MSF logos, and their location had been communicated to and was known by the Israeli military,” it wrote on X. World Health Organisation chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus slammed the attack. “Attacks on health facilities, health workers and humanitarian personnel in #Gaza are outrageous and unacceptable,” he posted on X. The IDF denied targeting a hospital or damaging medical infrastructure. The Israeli military has regularly targeted health facilities in the besieged Palestinian enclave. The latest attack comes amid a series of Israeli strikes targeting senior Hamas security officials in Gaza. On Wednesday, an Israeli air strike killed Mohammad Abuelouf, a Hamas colonel who headed the group’s internal security service in northern Gaza, along with his wife and two daughters at their apartment in Gaza City’s Beach refugee camp. On November 24, Israeli air strikes killed at least three people in Gaza, including Adel Al-Helo, a worker with the UN Palestinian refugee agency (UNRWA), according to the agency and local health officials. Al-Helo was working near a water well in Jabalia refugee camp when the strike hit. UNRWA said its staff were carrying out routine duties related to the well’s operations. The agency said three other people were wounded in the attack. In a separate strike later that day, two people were killed when an Israeli air strike targeted a vehicle in western Gaza City, medics said.

items.title: Obi, Makinde, Dino, others embrace at Dunamis Church
items.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, and Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, on Friday attended an all-night service at the headquarters of Dunamis International Gospel Centre (DIGC) in Abuja, where they joined other political figures in prayers for Nigeria and the peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections. Also present at the service were African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain, Dino Melaye, and an aide to Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori. The service, held at the church’s Glory Dome, formed part of activities marking the 30th anniversary of Dunamis, founded in November 1996 by Pastor Paul Enenche and his wife, Becky, both medical doctors turned pastors. The anniversary celebration featured the church’s annual week-long Kingdom Power and Glory World Conference (KPGWC), with this year’s edition themed, “Opened Heaven”. The conference attracted delegates from 82 countries, including Nigeria. At about 1 a.m. on Saturday, Enenche invited Obi, Makinde and Melaye to the altar for a special prayer session for Nigeria. They were joined by Oborevwori’s aide, who represented the All Progressives Congress (APC), and another church member representing the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). During the session, Enenche asked the five representatives to hold hands as he led the congregation in prayers anchored on Job 42:10. The prayer points included a plea for God’s perfect will to prevail in Nigeria, and for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct the 2027 elections fairly. The congregation also prayed for the smooth functioning of electoral systems and equipment, including the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as reliable internet connectivity during the elections. They further prayed for credible elections without bloodshed, crisis or post-election violence. Before the prayer session, the church’s South-South Coordinator, David Majiyebo, announced the presence of Melaye, Makinde, Obi and a former government minister, drawing a loud ovation from worshippers. After the session, which lasted less than 15 minutes, Enenche reminded the politicians that earthly life was temporary and that everyone would eventually stand before God to account for how they used the power entrusted to them. He also noted that genuine churches accommodate members with different political affiliations. Enenche subsequently asked the political representatives to shake hands and embrace one another as a demonstration of unity and the absence of bitterness. The politicians exchanged handshakes and embraces without making speeches. The pastor later asked the congregation whether the joint prayer session was good for Nigeria, and the worshippers responded in the affirmative. items.title: Fire guts Opebi Methodist Church, CAN seeks support
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Property worth millions of naira has been destroyed after fire partially gutted the Methodist Church Nigeria, Cathedral of Peace and Excellence, in Opebi, Ikeja, Lagos State. The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Lagos State Chapter, has expressed concern over the incident, describing it as a painful development for the Methodist congregation. The fire, which reportedly started in the church’s media room on the gallery late Wednesday night, caused significant damage to sections of the cathedral. The damage included the destruction of the church’s Allen organ, damage to the choir gallery and the collapse of about one-third of the roof. However, no life was lost and no injury was reported in the incident. The Permanent Secretary of the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA), Dr. Femi Oke-Osanyintolu, attributed the fire to an electrical surge in the agency’s preliminary assessment. He said the agency’s response team arrived at the scene about 10 minutes after receiving a distress call and worked alongside the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service and the Lagos Neighbourhood Safety Corps to contain the blaze. According to him, emergency responders successfully extinguished the fire and completed dampening operations to prevent a possible re-ignition. Oke-Osanyintolu said LASEMA subsequently declared the scene safe. He advised religious organisations, residents and business owners to conduct regular electrical inspections, ensure proper wiring and use certified electrical fittings to prevent similar incidents. Meanwhile, CAN, in a statement issued on Friday and signed by its Director of State Issues and Social Welfare, Rev. Stephen Oyinlola, sympathised with its Lagos State Chairman, Bishop Stephen Adegbite, the church leadership and members of the congregation. The association commended the church staff, sympathisers and emergency responders for their intervention, which helped prevent further destruction. CAN urged the congregation to remain steadfast in faith, while appealing to Christians, corporate organisations, individuals and other well-meaning Nigerians to support efforts to restore the affected sections of the cathedral. It expressed confidence that the church would recover from the incident and continue its religious and community services. items.title: L’Italie finance un projet de formation des jeunes tunisiens dans le tourisme
items.description: Le projet «Destination Emploi», financé par la Coopération italienne en Tunisie et mis en œuvre par la Fondation Avsi et Oxfam, en collaboration avec des partenaires italiens et tunisiens, a pour objectif de promouvoir l’emploi des jeunes par la formation professionnelle et contribuer au développement d’un secteur touristique innovant, responsable et durable. Il s’agit de former des compétences concrètes pour une insertion professionnelle stable. L’ambassadeur d’Italie à Tunis, Alessandro Prunas, et la directrice du bureau régional de l’Agence italienne pour la coopération au développement (AICS), Isabella Lucaferri, ont visité, le 26 novembre 2026, l’école de formation professionnelle aux métiers du tourisme de Tozeur, qui participe à cette initiative. Grâce à ce projet, 20 jeunes Tunisiens suivent des formations en pâtisserie et en service d’étage, acquérant ainsi des compétences techniques et transversales. À l’issue de leur formation, les bénéficiaires effectueront des stages au sein d’établissements hôteliers locaux, afin de faciliter leur entrée sur le marché du travail, explique l’ambassade d’Italie à Tunis. «La formation professionnelle est l'un des piliers du partenariat italo-tunisien. La Tunisie peut compter sur des structures de formation de qualité et sur un capital humain extraordinaire» , a déclaré M. Prunas, ajoutant que «l’Italie est fière d’accompagner la Tunisie dans l’élaboration de parcours de formation qui offrent aux jeunes des compétences concrètes, en adéquation avec les besoins des entreprises locales, et qui favorisent une insertion professionnelle stable et durable» . Lancé en octobre 2024, le projet «Destination Emploi» couvre également les zones d’Ain Draham, de Monastir et de Djerba. Il implique, parmi d’autres partenaires, Leaders International, la Fédération tunisienne de l’hôtellerie, l’Université Luiss Guido Carli et l’Association italienne pour le tourisme responsable (AITR). L’initiative vise à renforcer les liens entre le système de formation et le tissu entrepreneurial, à promouvoir l’emploi et l’auto-entrepreneuriat — en accordant une attention particulière aux jeunes, aux femmes et aux groupes vulnérables — et à contribuer ainsi à créer des alternatives concrètes à la migration irrégulière grâce au développement des économies locales. L’article L’Italie finance un projet de formation des jeunes tunisiens dans le tourisme est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Driver, student injured as armed men open fire on students’ bus in Charsadda
items.description: CHARSADDA: A driver and a student were injured when armed men allegedly opened fire on a coaster carrying students of Institute of Computer and Management Sciences (ICMS) College in the limits of Charsadda’s Nisatta police station late Friday night, police said. According to Station House Officer (SHO) Nisatta Khan Zaib, two vehicles carrying around 70 students were returning from a recreational trip to Murree when the incident occurred. The vehicles were travelling on GT Road after the motorway was closed and had reached the Nisatta area, he said. SHO Zaib told Dawn that the firing stemmed from a dispute between two students during the trip. He said a case had been registered against two nominated suspects, while several people had been arrested in connection with the incident. According to the coaster driver, who is the complainant in the case, a minor altercation had taken place between students during the trip. On their way back, the suspects, along with their accomplices, allegedly intercepted the vehicle and opened fire. The firing left the driver and a student with bullet wounds. They were taken to hospital, where the driver was later referred to Peshawar for further treatment. The complainant further alleged that the armed men had also tried to enter the vehicle but teachers standing near its door resisted them, preventing further harm to the students. Meanwhile, District Police Officer Rafatullah Khan took notice of the incident and directed the police to arrest the nominated suspects without delay. A special team, headed by Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Sardheri Bilal Haleem Khan and comprising SHO Zaib and other police officials, was formed to arrest the suspects. According to a statement issued by Charsadda police, raids were being conducted at various locations to apprehend those involved. A case was registered under Sections 324, 427 and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code. The president of the Private Colleges Association Charsadda, Sajjad Ali, and the president of the Council of Private Schools Association Charsadda, Mansoor Kausar Khan, condemned the firing. In a joint statement, they demanded an impartial inquiry and the immediate arrest of all those involved. They warned that all educational institutions in the district would be closed in protest if the suspects were not arrested and justice was not ensured. They also expressed concern over the safety of students and urged the police to take effective measures to prevent such incidents.

items.title: The Wellness cost of unreliable power
items.description: By Tochi Okafor The prolonged power cuts experienced over the last few months have brought back memories of growing up in the 1990s. I grew up in a low-cost neighbourhood, and incessant electricity outages were a regular feature of our lives. They drove me up the wall. I missed some of my favourite television programmes because, just when I was settling in to watch, the electricity would go off. My siblings and I also spent considerably more time on the balcony than we would have liked, simply because it was often the only place we could get some relief from the unbearable heat inside the house. I remember the frustration, the disappointment, and the general inconvenience of missing out on life’s little pleasures. But I also remember thinking that this was just a phase. Surely, things would improve as the country developed. Surely, more than two decades later, we would have moved past this. Yet here we are. Recent months serve as a stark reminder of the persistent issues facing Nigerians. Circumstances may have changed, and many households now have generators, inverters, and other alternatives, but the underlying struggle remains remarkably familiar. It is particularly disheartening to realise that something I experienced over 20 years ago is still consuming the time, money, and emotional energy of adults trying to build their lives today. I work in wellness education, and I believe we need to pay more attention to how our living and working environments influence our health. This is supported by an established public health framework known as the Social Determinants of Health. Recognised by the World Health Organization, this framework examines how the conditions in which people are born, grow, live and work shape their health outcomes. From that perspective, Nigeria’s unreliable electricity supply is not merely an infrastructure problem or an inconvenience. It is a public wellness issue, with consequences for our physical health, psychological well-being, and overall quality of life. One aspect I find particularly important is its effect on our sense of emotional safety. Emotional safety, in this context, is the sense of stability, predictability and control we derive from our immediate environment. It is the comfort of knowing that basic things will work when we need them to. We can return home, switch on the lights, cool our living spaces, prepare meals, charge our devices and get some rest without having to negotiate another interruption. When these ordinary expectations become uncertain, everyday life demands considerably more effort. People are forced to remain mentally prepared for disruptions that should not be a regular feature of daily living. Consider the Nigerian weather. It can be unbearably hot, yet you cannot confidently leave your air conditioner running. You switch on the generator, listen to it roar, monitor the fuel level and calculate how much longer you can afford to keep it running. A generator that should serve as an occasional backup has become an essential part of household infrastructure, with a recurring cost attached to its use. Then there is the noise. In densely populated neighbourhoods, generators have become part of the background soundtrack of everyday life. You hear them from neighbouring compounds, shops, offices and residential buildings. The World Health Organization identifies excessive environmental noise as a public health concern, associating prolonged exposure with sleep disturbance, annoyance, cardiovascular risks and impaired cognitive functioning. These are not trivial consequences. Sleep and recovery are fundamental to good health, yet many people have to contend with generator noise well into the night. There is also a more immediate danger. Poorly positioned generators can expose households to carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas that cannot be seen or smelled. In March 2025, The Guardian newspaper reported the deaths of a couple in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, following suspected carbon monoxide poisoning from generator fumes inside their apartment. It was a tragic reminder of the risks people can unknowingly face while trying to secure electricity for their homes. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention advises that generators should never be operated indoors, in garages or near doors, windows and vents. They should be positioned outdoors, at least 20 feet away from the home. The fact that households must increasingly depend on these machines makes generator safety an important public education issue, too. Even something as fundamental as nutrition becomes more complicated. I am particularly conscious of the relationship between food and wellness, and I know how much unreliable electricity can interfere with meal planning, preparation and storage. You have to consider what can be prepared quickly, what needs refrigeration and how long frozen food can remain safe without power. Food safety guidance from the US Department of Agriculture indicates that an unopened refrigerator generally keeps food cold for about four hours without electricity. A full freezer can maintain its temperature for approximately 48 hours, provided it remains closed. These are useful safety benchmarks, but they also illustrate why prolonged and unpredictable outages create practical challenges for households. You can plan your meals carefully, buy fresh ingredients and prepare food for the week, only to find yourself worrying about whether your refrigerator has maintained a safe temperature. For households that rely on refrigeration to preserve food, unreliable power introduces another layer of uncertainty into an activity as basic as feeding a family. The psychological burden is not always dramatic or immediately visible. Often, it accumulates through a series of small but repeated demands. You are anticipating the next outage, calculating the next fuel expense, rearranging your schedule and thinking about what needs to be charged before the electricity goes off again. Even when the power is available, there is sometimes an underlying awareness that it may not remain so. This constant need to anticipate and manage disruptions consumes mental energy. It can contribute to frustration, irritability, anxiety and exhaustion, particularly when people have little control over the circumstances creating the strain. This does not mean that every Nigerian living with unreliable electricity will develop a mental health condition. It means that people are being exposed to a persistent, avoidable source of stress, and that the cumulative burden deserves to be taken seriously. There is also the financial dimension. Money that could have gone towards savings, family needs, recreation or personal development is redirected towards fuel, generator maintenance and alternative power arrangements. People are spending more simply to maintain what should be a basic standard of living. In effect, the cost is not only what comes out of our pockets. It is also what we lose the opportunity to do with that money. For small business owners, the consequences are particularly difficult because unreliable electricity directly affects the cost of doing business. I have watched entrepreneurs express their frustration on social media about the rising cost of keeping their businesses operational. For many, alternative power is no longer an occasional expense. It is a significant and recurring operating cost. For a small business operating on tight margins, these decisions can determine whether the business remains profitable. The World Bank’s research on Nigeria’s business environment highlights the scale of the problem. Its reporting indicates that businesses experience substantial daily power interruptions, while generator ownership or shared access has become widespread. The World Bank also identifies unreliable electricity as a major constraint on private-sector productivity, with smaller businesses particularly vulnerable. When operating costs continually absorb resources that should support business development, there is less room to hire additional staff, improve equipment, invest in training or enhance customer experience. The entrepreneur is spending more energy keeping the business alive than building it. The same pressure affects Nigerians working remotely for international organisations and clients. A power interruption is rarely an acceptable reason to miss an important meeting or deliver work late. People therefore invest in inverters, generators, mobile internet alternatives or temporary workspaces just to maintain professional reliability. There is something particularly unfair about having to work twice as hard to remain productive because the infrastructure supporting your work cannot be relied upon. We encourage people to eat well, but reliable food storage cannot always be guaranteed. We promote adequate sleep, yet some people spend portions of their nights managing generators or trying to sleep through excessive heat and noise. We encourage entrepreneurship, productivity and economic participation, while the infrastructure that supports these activities remains unreliable. This is why I believe wellness conversations must extend beyond individual behaviour. Personal responsibility matters, but it cannot compensate indefinitely for an environment that makes healthy choices unnecessarily difficult. Of course, individual alternatives have their place. Solar panels, inverters and other off-grid solutions can reduce dependence on the national grid. However, these options require significant upfront investment, making them inaccessible to many households and small businesses. Even for those who can afford them, practical barriers remain. Tenants may be unable to install solar panels or make the necessary modifications to rented properties because of restrictions imposed by landlords. Access to reliable electricity is therefore also connected to affordability, housing arrangements and the ability of ordinary people to improve their living conditions. We cannot make individual citizens solely responsible for resolving a systemic infrastructure failure. Black out as charactriesed by lack of effective power (electricity) supply in Nigeria The government must treat reliable electricity as a fundamental development priority, with sustained attention to generation, transmission and distribution. There must also be greater accountability across the electricity value chain. Some of the issues that deserve attention include: Transparency: Clear and accessible reporting of power interruptions, grid failures and restoration timelines. Accountability: Greater responsibility from electricity distribution companies, including fair billing that reflects the quality and consistency of service delivered. Consumer protection: Better provisions for tenants and homeowners who want to adopt alternative energy solutions. Affordability: Accessible financing and policies that make solar and other reliable energy alternatives more attainable for households and small businesses. Infrastructure investment: Long-term investment in the generation, transmission and distribution systems required to deliver dependable electricity. This is not simply about having enough power to operate televisions, air conditioners and other household appliances. It is about allowing people to live, work, raise families and run businesses without the unnecessary burden of constantly finding ways around a problem that should be addressed at a systemic level. We must expand how we measure the cost of unreliable electricity. Megawatts, business losses and fuel expenditure are important indicators, but they do not tell the whole story. We must also account for disrupted sleep, financial anxiety, compromised food storage, environmental noise, safety risks and the emotional exhaustion of living with persistent uncertainty. A functional electricity system will not solve every wellness challenge Nigeria faces. But it will remove a significant and entirely unnecessary source of strain from people’s everyday lives. I think back to that little girl in the 1990s, sitting through another power outage, frustrated that she would miss her favourite television programme and retreating to the balcony with her siblings to escape the heat. She had every reason to believe that things would be better by the time she grew up. More than two decades later, I find myself having the same conversations about electricity, only now the stakes are considerably higher. Nigerians have not accepted this situation. We have survived it, and survival is not the same as living well. Sometimes, what people need is not another wellness lecture, another productivity hack or another motivational speech. Sometimes, they simply need the lights to stay on. The post The Wellness cost of unreliable power appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: APC, APGA stakeholders unite for Tinubu’s re-election in Anambra
items.description: Stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) in Orumba South Local Government Area of Anambra State have agreed to work together to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. The stakeholders also pledged to support Governor Chukwuma Charles Soludo’s position backing Tinubu’s second-term ambition. The resolution was reached at a joint stakeholders’ meeting held on Saturday, November 28, 2026, and convened by the Chairman of Orumba South Local Government, Hon. Shedrack Azubuike, in collaboration with Booth 2 Booth with Bola Tinubu, an APC support group led by its National Coordinator, Mr Ikechukwu Madu. At the meeting, the stakeholders agreed to strengthen political cooperation, unity and mutual understanding between the two parties, stressing the importance of working across party lines in pursuit of shared political and developmental interests. A major outcome of the meeting was the decision to support Soludo’s position on Tinubu’s re-election and mobilise grassroots support across Orumba South. To achieve this, the stakeholders resolved to establish a joint APC–APGA mobilisation committee to coordinate political engagement and grassroots mobilisation across the 18 wards of the local government area. They also agreed to promote peaceful political coexistence, political tolerance and constructive engagement, while sustaining regular consultations and collaborative initiatives for the development of Orumba South. The stakeholders commended Azubuike and Madu for initiating the engagement, describing the meeting as an opportunity to strengthen cooperation among political stakeholders and establish a common platform around shared objectives. Those present included the Deputy National Coordinator of Booth 2 Booth, Mr Jafar Abdulahi Ibrahim; the group’s Anambra State Coordinator, Mr Paschal Candle; and the APC Anambra State Organising Secretary, Mr Izuchukwu Okeke. The meeting ended with a reaffirmation of the stakeholders’ commitment to sustained APC–APGA cooperation, support for Soludo’s position on Tinubu’s re-election and grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The post 2027: APC, APGA stakeholders unite for Tinubu’s re-election in Anambra appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Maroc : transportée à dos de mulet, elle met 5 heures pour accéder aux soins
items.description: Le Maroc de Mohammed VI est irrémédiablement incorrigible. La dernière sortie médiatique du ministre marocain de l'industrie, Ryad Mezzour, peut laisser pantois. Et pour cause, ce membre de l'exécutif affirme toute honte bue que le système de santé marocain est « meilleur » que celui du Canada. Rien que ça ! Cette affirmation des plus saugrenues est vite balayée par le revers de l'index, par une scène tout aussi surréaliste, mais totalement tangible, observée à Tata, un coin reculé du Maroc profond. Récit d'un calvaire pesant, loin des hallucinations de Ryad Mezzour. Maroc : cinq heures de trajet pour accéder aux soins La scène s’est déroulée mardi dans le hameau d’Ighil Nikran, dans la province de Tata. Faute de route praticable, les habitants ont été contraints de transporter une jeune femme de 21 ans, souffrant de violentes douleurs abdominales, sur le dos d’un mulet. Les inondations, qui rendent l’accès au village difficile depuis près de deux mois, ont une nouvelle fois privé ses habitants d’un accès normal aux soins. وزير الصناعة والتجارة: قطاع الصحة بالمغرب أفضل من كندا #كندا #المغرب #الصحة #viral https://t.co/RNREohiCk4 — Hespress هسبريس (@hespress) November 21, 2026 Il aura fallu cinq heures à la jeune femme pour rejoindre le dispensaire le plus proche. Partie à 8 heures, elle n’y est arrivée qu’à 13 heures, après un trajet particulièrement éprouvant. Une vidéo diffusée sur les réseaux sociaux témoigne de cette évacuation pour le moins dramatique. Voir cette publication sur Instagram Une publication partagée par يابلادي yabiladi (@yabiladi.ar) Pour son père, Abdallah Laghrini, cette journée restera un souvenir douloureux. Prévenu par son épouse alors qu’il se trouvait loin du domicile familial, il a suivi avec inquiétude le déplacement de sa fille avant de la retrouver à son arrivée. « J’ai cru que j’allais perdre ma fille », confie-t-il. « Quand je suis arrivé et que je l’ai entendue crier de douleur, j’ai fondu en larmes : Je ne pouvais rien faire », a-t-il confié au média Yabiladi. Mohamed El Krini, président de l’Association Tifaouine pour le développement et l’action sociale à Ighil Nikran, indique que les douleurs avaient commencé dès 4 heures du matin. La route goudronnée se trouvant à une dizaine de kilomètres du hameau, l’ambulance n’a pas pu atteindre le village et a dû attendre la patiente pour assurer son transfert. Après une première étape à Alougoum, la jeune femme a été orientée vers Foum Zguid, où elle a été examinée par un médecin généraliste. Un isolement qui perdure malgré les promesses L’épisode met une nouvelle fois en évidence les difficultés auxquelles sont confrontés les habitants d’Ighil Nikran, particulièrement durant la saison des pluies. Les crues coupent régulièrement les accès au hameau, compliquant aussi bien les déplacements des familles que la scolarisation des enfants. Les villageois affirment avoir longtemps pris en charge eux-mêmes la remise en état de la piste après les intempéries. Mais face à l'ampleur des dégâts, ils ne sont désormais plus en mesure d'assurer ces réparations. Leurs démarches auprès des autorités locales sont, selon eux, restées sans réponse concrète. À ces difficultés s’ajoute l’absence de raccordement au réseau électrique. Les habitants disposaient auparavant d’une installation solaire mise en place dans le cadre d’un partenariat avec une organisation. Depuis la fin de cette convention, il y a dix ans, ils ont dû revenir à un éclairage rudimentaire. Des déclarations ministérielles à l’épreuve des faits Cette situation prend une dimension particulière au regard des déclarations récentes du ministre marocain de l'industrie, qui affirmait, il y a quelques jours, que le système sanitaire de son pays était meilleur que celui du Canada. Une affirmation qui contraste avec les difficultés rencontrées par les habitants d’Ighil Nikran, pour lesquels accéder à une simple consultation médicale peut nécessiter plusieurs heures de déplacement dans des conditions particulièrement pénibles. Entre enclavement, précarité énergétique et difficultés d’accès aux soins, le quotidien de ce hameau met en lumière les disparités persistantes derrière les discours officiels sur les performances du pays. items.title: Airlines losing passengers to travel stress, SITA warns
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Global air transport technology company, SITA, has said travel-related stress is discouraging people from travelling, leading to lost bookings and revenue for airlines. SITA’s 2026 Passenger IT Insights said a survey of nearly 8,000 travellers across 24 countries, four in 10 (42 per cent) have decided against taking a trip because they expected the experience to be too stressful. However, SITA’s Chief Executive Officer, David Lavorel, said the air transport industry could recover bookings and revenue lost to travel-related stress by deploying technology to give passengers greater visibility and control at every stage of their journeys. The survey also found that passengers increasingly expect technology to provide solutions, with eight in 10 believing it can reduce the stress associated with air travel. For airlines, the lost bookings are particularly significant because they involve some of their most valuable customers. Six in 10 frequent flyers have abandoned plans to travel because of anticipated stress. More than half of travellers under 30, the next generation of frequent flyers, have also done so. These two groups are also the most confident that technology can make air travel less stressful, with 89 per cent of frequent flyers and 86 per cent of travellers under 30 expressing confidence in its potential. Lavorel said: “Every trip we win back is a seat filled, a parking space sold and a coffee bought. Travellers are telling us where the stress comes from: delays, queues and worrying about their bags. Most of it comes down to not knowing what happens next. When airlines, airports, ground handlers and border agencies share what they know, passengers can see what is coming before they have to ask.” The post Airlines losing passengers to travel stress, SITA warns appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CDA seals Fazl’s Islamabad residence after 'foreign' owner's CNIC cancelled
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Saturday sealed the Islamabad residence of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman after the identity card of the property’s legal owner was cancelled. The move comes amid continuing tensions between the JUI-F and the federal government. A notice affixed on the property gate on Thursday said the building has been sealed by CDA’s Building & Housing Control “on account of cancellation of ownership”. A CDA notice affixed on a gate of JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s residence in Islamabad on Nov 28, 2026. — via Kashif Abbasi CDA’s Building & Housing Control swung into action a day after the deputy director for CDA’s Estate Management-I ordered sealing of the property due to the change of title being cancelled. In an order dated Nov 27, the deputy director for CDA’s Estate Management-I noted that the owner, Amanullah, son of Muhammad Younus, had been “identified as a foreign national and his Pakistani Computerised National Identity Card (CNIC) had accordingly been cancelled”. “In exercise of the powers delegated by the Authority to the member (Estate) and after consideration of the available record and observance of the prescribed process, the change of title granted in favour of Mr Aman Ullah s/o Muhammad Younas, […] has been CANCELLED with immediate effect,” read the order, available with Dawn . It directed the director general of the CDA’s Building & Housing Control Department to seal the property, adding that he could seek assistance from CDA formations and the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration, if required. “Consequential legal action shall be taken by Directorate of Estate Management-1,” it added. The CDA order noted that the focal person for Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) Illegal Foreigners’ Repatriation Plan (IFRP), in a letter dated Nov 25, also confirmed the cancellation of Amanullah’s Pakistani CNIC “following verification by Nadra and requested initiation of appropriate legal proceedings in respect of immovable properties reportedly acquired by him in Islamabad”. CDA highlighted that Amanullah had been given an opportunity of hearing as a show-cause notice was issued to him on Nov 25 to appear personally before the CDA member for Estate on Nov 26 and explain why the change of title in his favour should not be cancelled. The CDA said Amanullah could not be found at the “subject property for personal service of the notice, whereupon the notice was duly pasted at the premises of the subject property” to communicate the proceedings to him. However, Amanullah allegedly failed to appear before the CDA Estate member on Nov 26, nor “did he avail himself of the opportunity of hearing to rebut the allegations or produce any valid identity document or prior written permission of the competent government” for acquiring the property. CDA had also issued notice against the same property on Oct 30 for placing a generator outside and for alleged illegal/unauthorised construction. ‘Violation of prescribed transfer requirements’ According to the CDA order, the matter regarding Amanullah’s nationality and identity credentials was brought to its notice through “official communications received from various government agencies”, including the Office of the District Magistrate, the focal person for IFRP, ICT and the National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra). It noted that as per a Nadra letter, Amanullah had originally obtained his CNIC on the basis of his parents’ CNIC, whereas “discrepancies had been observed in the family record, including the existence of two CNICs of his late father, Muhammad Younas”. The order said that subsequent verification by Nadra established that the identity document furnished by Amanullah “for the purpose of obtaining change of title in respect of the subject property was not a valid Pakistani CNIC and had been cancelled by the competent authority, thereby rendering the mandatory identity requirement for processing the change of title unfulfilled”. It stated that under Chapter 6 of the CDA Property Manual, which requires producing a valid CNIC, furnishing an invalid identity document constituted a “material violation of the prescribed transfer requirements and vitiates the administrative process through which the change of title was obtained”. The CDA also cited Section 3 of the Foreigners Act 1946, which empowers the government to regulate the acquisition of property by foreigners, stating that a 1984 order under it provided that no foreigner shall “acquire land or any interest in land or landed property in Pakistan except with the previous permission in writing of the federal government or of the provincial government”. “No such permission has been produced or placed on the record of the Authority in respect of the subject property,” the order maintained. Consequently, the CDA’s Estate Wing initiated proceedings to cancel the change of title granted in Amanullah’s favour, the document added. Fazl-govt rift Fazl had criticised the Centre for imposing governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and making the then-PTI provincial government non-functional. The JUI-F chief also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the PML-N and PTI governments. Tensions escalated when Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights, resulting in the veteran politician and key federal ministers exchanging harsh remarks . In recent weeks, PPP Chairman Bilawal-Bhutto Zardari — a key ally of the ruling PML-N — has voiced his support for Fazl and condemned the “government’s actions” against him. Last week, police and Federal Constabulary (FC) personnel deployed to protect Fazl and other members of his family were withdrawn from the residences they guarded in Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan. A JUI-F spokesman had confirmed the withdrawal, alleging that Fazl’s Islamabad residence had been cordoned off by capital police and that security personnel had harassed visitors. He also claimed that the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad had been besieged by police. An Islamabad police official, however, said only one police guard had been withdrawn. The JUI-F chief’s son has also come under scrutiny from the anti-graft watchdog, with the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) summoning former federal communications minister Asad Mahmood over alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure. Mahmood skipped two consecutive summonses issued for Nov 10 and 14, according to a NAB source. The JUI-F staged protests in parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Nov 7 against a “coordinated character assassination campaign” targeting Fazl. Party leaders and workers condemned the alleged drone surveillance of his residence and the circulation of footage on social media, demanding an impartial investigation and action against those responsible. On Tuesday, Fazl claimed he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to prevent him from attending a multiparty conference hosted by the Lahore High Court Bar Association. On Thursday, authorities barred the JUI-F chief and eight other leaders of his party from entering, residing or remaining in Sargodha — where the JUI-F planned to hold a rally that day — for 30 days. Despite the restriction, Fazl said in a video message that he was setting out for Sargodha. The next day, hours after Fazl claimed that he was under arrest, Lahore Capital City Police Officer Bilal Siddique Kamyana denied that the politician had been taken into custody. The JUI-F also claimed that several party activists and workers had been arrested and booked across Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as the party staged protests at various locations on Thursday and Friday .

items.title: US, Italy disruptions expose urgency of Nigeria’s air navigation upgrade
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Following recent air traffic disruptions in the United States and Italy, linked to ageing infrastructure and telecommunications failures, calls have grown for Nigeria to urgently upgrade its air navigation infrastructure and equipment to avert similar incidents Many have warned that similar disruptions in the country could cause enormous financial losses, particularly for airlines already grappling with high operating costs, foreign exchange pressures, surging jet fuel prices and heavy taxation, while leaving passengers stranded and disrupt crucial travel plans. Beyond the immediate impact on flight schedules, they said airlines could incur additional costs from refunding affected passengers and providing care and assistance to those stranded. The concerns came after the unexpected incident in the United States on Friday, November 13, 2026, when the Federal Aviation Administration, FAA, imposed a nationwide ground stop that lasted several hours due to a telecommunications and equipment outage. United States Transportation Secretary, Sean Duffy, who attributed the problem to ageing infrastructure and instability in the country’s air traffic control radar and communications systems, said the wider economic impact of the disruption could run into billions of dollars. The communications failure affected all 22 air route traffic control centres, which guide aircraft across the country, leaving more than 10,000 flights delayed and at least 4,000 cancelled, according to FlightAware. The four largest US airlines, including American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and Southwest Airlines, could also suffer a combined $345m hit to their pre-tax earnings, according to brokerage firm Bernstein. Italy also experienced a major disruption in October, although the cause was different. An overnight fault in the geographic data transmission network supporting the country’s air traffic control system disrupted flight operations across several airports. The resulting delays and cancellations affected airports nationwide, including Rome Fiumicino, Milan, Bergamo, Naples, Venice, Palermo, Cagliari and Trieste. While intercontinental departures were prioritised, shorter-distance flights faced more interruptions. Urgent Against this backdrop, many aviation professionals across the country have said the need to accelerate the upgrade of the country’s air navigation infrastructure before similar failures occur cannot be over emphasised. Some of the equipment requiring attention include the Total Radar Coverage of Nigeria, TRACON, communication networks and navigation beacons. While the Nigerian Airspace Management Agency, NAMA, has identified some of the equipment as obsolete, lacking spare parts and operating beyond its expected lifespan, others have been described as overstretched. For instance, the Nigerian Air Traffic Controllers Association, NATCA, which has about 400 members, some of whom are in NAMA, has consistently raised concerns over the state of the country’s communication and surveillance equipment. At the association’s 55th Annual General Meeting, held recently in Lagos and themed: ‘Beyond Silos to Synergy: Shaping the Future of Nigerian Air Traffic Management,’ it further deepened the call for urgent investment in critical infrastructure. President of NATCA, Mr Edino Amos, lamented that 2026 had been a difficult year for air traffic controllers, ATCOs, saying there had been no significant improvement in communication and surveillance infrastructure despite the challenges confronting personnel across the country. While acknowledging announced approvals and procurement milestones, he said these were yet to translate into tangible improvements in the equipment available to controllers at their consoles. Steps taken Amos said the association had engaged relevant government institutions and aviation authorities in a bid to secure the necessary improvements. He said: “NATCA has sought a high-level presentation of its position to the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, the National Counter Terrorism Centre, the Office of the National Security Adviser and the Management of NAMA. The Association has also submitted a memorandum to the National Assembly on aviation funding reform, in which we make the case that safety-critical infrastructure requires predictable and ring-fenced funding. “It is with a deep sense of responsibility that I state that this frustrating engagement is pushing the association towards considering the withdrawal of our services, should there be no clear strategic plan for the total overhaul of communication and surveillance infrastructure in Nigeria.” He identified several areas requiring urgent attention, including improving airspace safety, reducing economic waste, enhancing profitability for airline operators and attracting more airlines to Nigerian airspace. He said: “Minister, we make this call not as a threat, but as patriots who sit daily before screens and failing frequencies to keep this country safe.” Welfare Amos also said infrastructure upgrades must be matched with improved staff welfare, adding that a motivated workforce was essential to achieving optimal performance. He lamented that, at the prevailing exchange rate, an average air traffic controller could barely make ends meet. He said: “Inflation has since eroded the value of that review. NATCA has therefore engaged management on the review of the ATC Aeromedical Allowance; and the review of the Rating Allowance, which is long overdue.” Reliability The call for improved air navigation infrastructure has also featured in discussions among other aviation professionals. At the 2026 Annual General Meeting of the National Association of Air Traffic Engineers, NAAE, held in Jos, Director of Aerodrome and Airspace Standards at the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, Ahmad Abba, said there is a need for ageing infrastructure to be addressed, alongside reliable power supply, preventive maintenance and tested contingency arrangements in the air transport sector. While speaking on the theme: ‘Optimising CNS/ATM Through Enhanced Training, Operation and Regulatory Compliance,’ Abba identified cybersecurity threats and interference with satellite navigation signals, including jamming and spoofing, as risks requiring coordinated action by aviation stakeholders and relevant national authorities. He said reliable air navigation services are essential not only for airspace safety but also for the growth and sustainability of Nigerian airlines, passenger confidence and the long-term development of the aviation sector. Although he welcomed efforts to modernise Nigeria’s air navigation infrastructure, including the planned overhaul of the TRACON system and the introduction of Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast, ADS-B, capability, he said infrastructure projects must incorporate personnel training, maintenance arrangements, spare parts and safety assessments from the outset. He said: “Modern equipment matters. But equipment alone does not create a safe airspace. Competent people, disciplined operations and effective regulation do.” The post US, Italy disruptions expose urgency of Nigeria’s air navigation upgrade appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: United ATS veut faire de la Tunisie un pôle de formation aéronautique
items.description: La disponibilité de compétences locales, d’infrastructures technologiques et de personnel spécialisé pourrait permettre au pays de devenir un pôle régional voire même un hub mondial pour la formation aéronautique. La pénurie de personnel qualifié dans le secteur de la navigation aérienne et du contrôle du trafic aérien «représente un défi pour l’Europe, les États-Unis et de nombreux autres pays, dans un contexte de croissance du trafic aérien et de demande croissante en compétences spécialisées» , a souligné, dans une déclaration à Agenzia Nova , Ghofran Ben Ameur, coordinateur de la formation chez United ATS Tunisie, identifiant ce besoin international comme une opportunité pour le développement du secteur en Tunisie et en Afrique. La situation en Europe confirme également la dimension internationale de ce problème. Selon l’Organisation européenne pour la sécurité de la navigation aérienne (Eurocontrol), plusieurs centres de contrôle du trafic aérien continuent de faire face à des difficultés structurelles en matière de capacité, dues notamment à une pénurie de contrôleurs. En 2025, les retards liés à la gestion du trafic aérien sont restés élevés, mettant en évidence la nécessité de renforcer le recrutement et la formation de personnel hautement spécialisé. La disponibilité de compétences locales, d’infrastructures technologiques et de personnel spécialisé pourrait, en effet, permettre à la Tunisie de devenir un pôle régional de formation aéronautique. C’est dans cette optique que s’inscrit United ATS Tunisia, nouvelle structure de formation inaugurée cette semaine au quartier du Lac, à Tunis, en présence d’autorités chargées de la sécurité, ainsi que de représentants institutionnels et diplomatiques. Une telle participation témoigne également de l’intérêt des pays africains pour le développement de parcours de formation et de coopération dans le secteur de l’aviation. Savoir-faire, technicité et coûts compétitifs «La Tunisie dispose des compétences et des conditions nécessaires pour développer un centre de formation aéronautique capable de répondre aussi à la demande des pays de la région» , explique au média italien Sofiane Bejaoui, instructeur en chef chez United ATS Tunisia. Selon lui, cette structure permet de «proposer sur le marché local, à des coûts compétitifs et en monnaie nationale, des services qui sont actuellement achetés à l’étranger» . Pour établir une comparaison, M. Bejaoui cite le centre français qui fait référence dans le secteur, tout en mettant en avant les compétences aéronautiques, les instructeurs qualifiés et les professionnels dotés d’une expérience internationale présents en Tunisie ; des atouts qui attirent déjà des clients venus d’Irak, de Libye et du Koweït. L’instructeur rappelle par ailleurs les activités de formation technique déjà menées au sein de divers centres internationaux et auprès d’entreprises du secteur aéronautique en Libye et en Égypte, «notamment des entités de l’aviation civile, telles que la compagnie libyenne Buraq» . L’objectif est donc d’accroître la capacité de formation en Tunisie et de l’ouvrir aux marchés africains et francophones. «La Tunisie vise à renforcer son rôle de hub régional pour la formation et l’innovation technologique dans le secteur de l’aviation, en ciblant les marchés des pays voisins, africains et francophones» , déclare Meriem Ben Othmen, directrice générale de United ATS Tunisia. Cette entreprise tunisienne à vocation internationale, issue du groupe United ATS, bénéficie de plus de 20 ans d’expérience à l’échelle mondiale. Le centre est spécialisé dans la formation à la navigation aérienne et au contrôle du trafic aérien ; il est agréé par la Direction générale de l’aviation civile relevant du ministère des Transports ainsi que par le ministère de la Formation professionnelle et de l’Emploi. Il est par ailleurs accrédité en tant que centre de formation par l’Organisation de l’aviation civile internationale (Oaci). La ​​structure dispose de salles équipées et de technologies de simulation reproduisant divers scénarios opérationnels dans le domaine de l’aviation. Elle est notamment dotée de simulateurs radar, d’approche et de tour de contrôle, permettant aux élèves de s’exercer à la gestion du trafic aérien et aux procédures opérationnelles. Des outils de simulation de vol ainsi que des environnements technologiques dédiés à la formation technique sont également disponibles. Le centre propose plus de 400 formations, conçues en fonction des besoins des pays partenaires ; il s’appuie sur des formateurs tunisiens et internationaux, ainsi que sur des équipements conformes aux normes internationales, précise Mme Ben Othman. L’ambition de l’entreprise dépasse le cadre de la formation : elle vise à créer une plateforme dédiée au transfert technologique et à la coopération internationale. C’est dans cette optique que s’inscrivent les partenariats noués avec la société Enova et le Réseau d’affaires tuniso-canadien (RATC), visant le développement de simulateurs et l’intégration de nouvelles technologies — y compris l’intelligence artificielle — au sein des activités liées à l’aviation. L’objectif est de valoriser les compétences locales et de renforcer la capacité de la Tunisie à desservir les marchés régionaux et africains. La robotique au cœur du métier La centralité de l’être humain face aux algorithmes, ainsi que l’importance d’intégrer des principes éthiques et des mesures de sécurité dans le développement de l’intelligence artificielle, ont été au cœur de l’intervention de Slim Saidani, cofondateur et vice-président de RATC. En s’appuyant sur la théorie des «intelligences multiples» du psychologue Howard Gardner, M. Saidani a souligné que la formation doit développer des compétences logiques, linguistiques et spatiales, notamment par le biais de simulateurs et d’outils technologiques. Le dirigeant a par ailleurs insisté sur le rôle crucial du jugement humain dans les processus décisionnels et dans la gestion des erreurs des systèmes automatisés, tout en évoquant la contribution canadienne au développement de l’apprentissage profond ( deep learning ) et l’attention portée à l’éthique au sein de l’intelligence artificielle. Un autre axe de collaboration concerne la robotique et l’intégration de systèmes intelligents dans les simulateurs. L’ingénieur-chercheur Amir Ismail explique que le modèle opérationnel d’Enova Robotics repose sur le concept de «robot en tant que service» (Robot-as-a-Service) : il ne s’agit pas simplement de vendre un robot à un client, mais de l’accompagner tout au long d’un processus continu de développement, de personnalisation, de mise à jour et d’assistance, en fonction de ses besoins spécifiques. Le partenariat avec United ATS vise, plus précisément, à développer une couche logicielle fondée sur l’intelligence artificielle destinée à être intégrée dans des simulateurs, avec des applications touchant notamment à la communication entre les robots et les opérateurs. L’objectif, ajoute M. Ismail, est d’ «identifier des solutions technologiques capables d’améliorer aussi bien les produits d’Enova Robotics que les simulateurs développés par United ATS» . «La robotique constitue notre cœur de métier, tandis que l’intelligence artificielle en représente le cerveau» , affirme le représentant d’Enova. Il souligne que la combinaison de ces deux technologies peut favoriser l’émergence de systèmes toujours plus autonomes, tout en reconnaissant les limites actuelles de l’intelligence artificielle et l’absence, à ce jour, d’une véritable intelligence artificielle générale (IAG). La formation de personnel spécialisé, le développement de simulateurs et le transfert technologique constituent ainsi les trois axes par lesquels United ATS entend contribuer au renforcement de la position tunisienne dans le secteur aéronautique, dans une perspective qui dépasse le marché national et vise la coopération avec des pays européens et africains. I. B. (avec Agenzia Nova ). L’article United ATS veut faire de la Tunisie un pôle de formation aéronautique est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: WWC 2027Q: Black Queens begin playoff tournament against Ecuador on November 28
items.description: Ghana will have another bite at 2027 Women’s World Cup qualification with the start of the interconfederation playoff tournament this weekend. The Black Queens get their campaign underway on Saturday evening when they take on Ecuador in the first of their three games for the tournament, with kickoff scheduled for 19:00 GMT. Kim Lars Bjorkegren’s side have another opportunity to end their wait for another World Cup appearance after missing automatic qualification following the defeat to Malawi in the quarterfinals of the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON). However, that did not end hopes of their quest to return to the global stage for the first time in twenty years, as they defeated Cote d’Ivoire to secure a place in the interconfederation playoff tournament. While the Black Queens would have wished for a simpler route, they made things complicated for themselves. Six nations – Ghana, South Africa, Ecuador, Uzbekistan, Chinese Taipei and Papua New Guinea – will compete for two places in the final phase of the playoffs, where they will join four countries from CONCACAF, CONMEBOL and UEFA to compete for the last three spots. Ghana get their campaign underway against Ecuador with head coach Bjorkegren highlighting the importance of his team starting right in the preliminary phase. “To win the first one will put us in a good position for the next two” Kim Lars Bjorkegren previews the Black Queens World Cup playoff tournament opener against Ecuador tomorrow #JoySports https://t.co/XhqgigQfeX — #JoySports (@JoySportsGH) November 27, 2026 The Queens head into the tie without the services of Doris Boaduwaa, Alice Kusi and Mukarama Abdulai, three players who have left a mark with their recent performances. Boaduwaa continues her recovery from a hamstring injury, while there are no explanations for the absence of Kusi and Mukarama, despite the latter scoring a brace in the Black Queens’ last game against Mauritius in the 2028 Olympic Games qualifiers. The team has been in Rabat since opening camp on Monday, with preparations taking place for the fixture. After the game on Saturday, the Black Queens will place Uzbekistan on December 1 and wrap it up against Papua New Guinea four days later. Bjorkegren’s side must finish as one of the top two to advance into the final phase of the playoffs.

items.title: ¿Qué tiempo hará el día de las elecciones generales del 29-N? El paraguas, solo en Galicia y Cantábrico
items.description: Mientras en las urnas se fragua el futuro de España en una jornada informativamente apasionante ante lo ajustado de los pronósticos , el tiempo de este domingo 29 de noviembre tendrá en cambio “poca chicha”, porque el día transcurrirá “en general tranquilo y estable, sin ninguna situación adversa”, según indica Rubén Del Campo, portavoz de la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet), en una predicción especial ampliada y con más detalle para EL PAÍS. Seguir leyendo ¿Cómo afecta el tiempo a la participación y a los resultados electorales? En España apenas hay estudios al respecto, salvo uno liderado por Joaquín Artés, que imparte Economía en la Universidad Complutense de Madrid. Este análisis, titulado The rain in Spain: Turnout and partisan voting in Spanish elections y que midió en concreto el impacto de las precipitaciones en las elecciones municipales entre 1987 y 2011, y concluye que la lluvia supone una disminución de la participación inferior a medio punto porcentual, con lo que puede bailar algún escaño, pero no producirse un vuelco. Esta investigación evidencia, además, que la lluvia beneficia a la derecha, porque afecta más a los que no están del todo convencidos de acudir a votar, como ocurre con el votante de izquierdas, tradicionalmente menos movilizado. Eso sí, lo que no se ha estudiado en España es el efecto del buen tiempo, como el que se espera, en la participación.

items.title: Ken Ashigbey urges mining industry to prioritise integrity, stewardship and community impact
items.description: The Convenor of the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining (MCAM), Ing. Kenneth Ashigbey, has called for Ghana’s mining industry to be judged not only by its production levels and economic contributions but also by its integrity, environmental responsibility, safety standards and impact on mining communities. He said the industry’s long-term success must be anchored in responsible practices that protect the environment, promote innovation, safeguard workers and ensure mineral wealth contributes meaningfully to sustainable development. Speaking at the 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards in Accra on Friday, November 27, Ing. Ashigbey said the sector must strive to build a reputation that reflects both economic performance and its commitment to society. “For me, the answer must include an industry recognised not only for its production and economic contribution but equally for its integrity, innovation, environmental stewardship, commitment to safety, and positive impact on our communities,” he said. He stressed that the mining industry’s achievements should be measured beyond production figures and financial returns, arguing that responsible mining, environmental protection and the welfare of host communities must remain central to its operations. Ing. Ashigbey said the sector’s future would depend on its ability to balance commercial success with ethical conduct, environmental sustainability and meaningful community development. Centenary should define industry’s legacy He said the industry’s forthcoming centenary would provide an important opportunity for stakeholders to reflect on its achievements, reassess its priorities and determine the legacy it wanted to leave for future generations. According to him, the milestone should be more than a ceremonial celebration of the sector’s history, but a moment to establish a renewed commitment to excellence and responsible mining. “Our centenary will therefore be more than a celebration, it will be an opportunity to excellency and define the legacy we wish to leave to the next generation,” he said. Ing. Ashigbey urged stakeholders to use the occasion to strengthen standards and promote practices that would ensure Ghana’s mineral resources were managed responsibly and their benefits sustained over time. He said the legacy of the industry should be reflected in the quality of environmental protection, the opportunities created for communities, the safety of workers and the sustainability of the country’s mining operations. Acknowledges collaboration with government and institutions The MCAM Convenor also acknowledged the contributions of government institutions, regulators, Parliament and other stakeholders to the progress of Ghana’s mining industry. He recognised the working relationship between the Ghana Chamber of Mines and the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, as well as the Ministry of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation. He also commended the Minerals Commission, the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), Parliament and other public institutions for their engagement and cooperation with the industry. Ing. Ashigbey said collaboration among industry players, government and regulatory institutions remained critical to ensuring the responsible development of Ghana’s mineral resources. He acknowledged that stakeholders might not always agree on every issue but said their engagements were guided by a common interest in sustainable mining and national development. “While we may not always agree on every issue, our engagements are guided by a shared commitment to sustainable development of Ghana’s mineral resources,” he said. He maintained that differences in perspectives should not undermine efforts to work together towards achieving common objectives, particularly in addressing challenges facing the mining sector. Calls for dialogue and mutual respect Ing. Ashigbey said mutual respect, open dialogue and constructive engagement were essential to strengthening relationships between mining companies, government agencies, regulators and other stakeholders. He said sustained collaboration would help build trust, address concerns and create a stronger foundation for the industry’s continued development. “We remain convinced that mutual respect, open dialogue and collaboration provide the strongest foundation for progress,” he said. He urged stakeholders to maintain constructive engagements and work collectively towards ensuring Ghana’s mineral resources were developed in a manner that delivered economic benefits while protecting the environment and improving the lives of communities. The 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards brought together key players in the mining sector to recognise excellence, innovation, responsible mining practices and contributions to the development of Ghana’s mineral industry.
