items.title: The Savannah Fruits Company, GIZ Ghana enter €1.3m PSInno partnership to strengthen women-led shea businesses in northern Ghana
items.description: The Head of Programme for the Private Sector and Innovation Promotion (PSInno) programme at GIZ Ghana, Arlett Stojanovic, says the German government has allocated funding to create jobs and increase incomes in northern Ghana through a new partnership to support shea collectors. The partnership brings together the German government, The Savannah Fruits Company and local communities. Speaking at the launch of the Shea RISE (Resilient Infrastructure for Shea Ecosystems) project, Ms Stojanovic described it as a very good recipe for success and a strong basis for the future. The partnership, under Shea RISE, involves the GIZ’s PSInno programme, in partnership with the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, and The Savannah Fruits Company. It aims to transform 16 cooperative-owned post-harvest centres into independent, well-run, women-led businesses. Shea supports about 16 million women across West Africa. By 2028, the project aims to bring 4,000 women collectors and processors into registered cooperatives and train 4,032 people, including 32 RISE Fellows. Sixteen of the trainees will become Centre Managers, with women expected to occupy at least 60 per cent of those positions. Ms Stojanovic said the project would help women earn income throughout the year. “I’m very happy that we have this project together that is looking at actually making your life a bit easier and increasing also the income. And the reason is that the German government has allocated some money to create jobs, to increase income, especially in the north of Ghana,” she said on Friday, November 27. “I mean, one thing that I personally like very much about the project is that it’s not just looking at shea and the post-harvest center for shea, but it’s actually having the ambition of creating income all-year round. So, you know, to turn it more into an enterprise and not just a benefit for those two, three months.” The Managing Director and Co-founder of The Savannah Fruits Company Ltd, Raphael Gonzalez, said the Shea RISE project would enable women to collect more nuts, receive immediate cash payments and work together in safer conditions. “It’s much more engaging because they don’t have to process the nuts and the whole thing at home. They go to pick the nuts, they bring it after a half day, five times more, and they get paid straight away, cash, and then they can do other things. And it comes at a time where it’s very welcome because that’s the beginning of the rainy season. They can use the money to do other things and also because after the dry season the reserves are a bit low, so they can buy food for the kids and so on. So, the fact that the youth are interested now is very positive because we get more quantity and better quality.” The’Savannah Fruits Company has powered rural entreprises enterprises to process and supply shea, baobab, coconut, soy, honey, cowpea and other natural ingredients to international markets through long-term investment, direct sourcing and committed market access. Speaking to JoyNews, Mariama Zakaria Magajia of the Nyeko Women’s Group said the support had made it easier for them to process shea. “We used to process it the traditional way which was very difficult. The machines have now made the work very easy and we are grateful,” she said. Meanwhile, the founder of Eco-Restore raised concerns about the cutting down of shea and other indigenous trees, warning that the practice was beginning to affect the supply of raw materials to factories. “We’re cutting down the shea and other trees and now we don’t even have enough crop in Ghana to feed our factories. So, with a couple of other Ghanaians, Senyon Pele and Zakaria Isahaku, we formed Eco-Restore in 2019 to make money growing back our indigenous trees. In just seven years we’ve now established over a million indigenous trees. We’ve worked in 70 communities across three regions.” The wider ambition is to expand this proven model to 90 centres in Northern Ghana, reaching an estimated 22,500 women shea collectors and processors. The project runs from October 2026 to October 2028. It is expected to transition 16 high-performing centres from the pilot into autonomous, formally governed, women-led and bankable cooperative enterprises, formalising around 4,000 women collectors and processors as cooperative members. Along the way, 32 young RISE Fellows will be trained and employed to help run the centres, biomass boilers and deshelling machines will be installed across all 16 centres, and all purchased volumes will be traced at batch level. The aim is to prove a practical, replicable model for shea’s first mile that communities can run and sustain on their own.

items.title: De Roubtzoff à Zoubeir Turki, les Tunisiennes au premier plan
items.description: Des œuvres des peintres Alexandre Roubtzoff (Saint-Pétersbourg, 1884 – Tunis, 1949), Yahia Turki (Constantinople 1902-Tunis 1969) et Zoubeir Turki provenant de collections tunisiennes seront présentées à la vente chez Millon, maison parisienne de vente aux enchères, les 8 et 14 décembre 2026, à l’Hôtel Drouot, salle 9. Roubtzoff veut garder la trace des traditions tunisiennes. Yahia Turki emprunte à l’impressionnisme pour peindre son pays. Zoubeir Turki puise dans ses souvenirs de la médina. Leurs portraits de femmes racontent ces différentes façons de regarder la Tunisie. Le tableau ‘‘Femmes préparant le couscous’’ , qui sera présenté à la vente le 14 décembre chez Millon, fera écho à deux portraits proposés le 8 décembre, dans la vente «Modernités arabes & africaines» . Roubtzoff : conserver les usages d’une Tunisie qui change Arrivé à Tunis en 1914, Roubtzoff s’intéresse aux femmes dans leurs activités quotidiennes. Ce choix le distingue de l’odalisque idéalisée d’une partie de la peinture orientaliste du XIX e siècle. Il cherche à documenter des coutumes : les costumes, les bijoux et les tatouages deviennent des éléments de connaissance de la société qu’il découvre. Son orientalisme prend ainsi une dimension ethnographique. Son souci du détail traduit aussi un attachement aux traditions. Dans un article publié en 1938 dans la revue Tunisie , il déplorera la modernisation du pays. Peindre lui permet de conserver l’image des usages auxquels il tient. Réalisé en 1915, un an après son arrivée à Tunis, Femmes préparant le couscous témoigne de cette démarche dès ses premières années tunisiennes. Les prénoms de Fatima et Mahbouba, inscrits en arabe, et les indications des séances de pose accompagnent son travail d’observation. Conservée par descendance dans une collection familiale tunisienne, cette toile de 80 × 98 cm sera présentée le 14 décembre, avec une estimation de 100 000 à 150 000 euros. Sa présentation intervient deux jours après l’ouverture à Cannes de l’exposition «Alexandre Roubtzoff — Sous le soleil de Carthage.» Yahia Turki : la peinture moderne pour représenter son pays Yahia Turki connaît les mêmes rues et les mêmes traditions, mais son projet se construit autrement. Lors de ses séjours parisiens, il découvre l’impressionnisme. Il en retient une touche libre et une palette vive, qu’il met au service de sujets tunisiens : les habitants de la médina, les rassemblements, les fêtes et la vie domestique. Il associe ainsi les recherches de la peinture européenne à son expérience du pays. Cette démarche fait de lui un pionnier d’une modernité tunisienne, qu’il défendra aussi comme président de l’École de Tunis à partir de 1956. Ses portraits accordent une large place aux femmes de différentes conditions sociales, des bédouines aux citadines et aux employées de maison. Le Portrait de bédouine allongée , issu de l’ancienne collection Marcelle Cohen, née à Tunis, appartient à cet ensemble. Il sera proposé le 8 décembre, avec une estimation de 10 000 à 15 000 euros. Zoubeir Turki : faire revivre les personnages du Tunis de son enfance Chez Zoubeir Turki, le portrait passe aussi par le souvenir. Dans un hommage publié en 2009, l’ancien ministre de la Culture Chedli Klibi décrit un artiste qui retrouve de mémoire les citadins fréquentés dans sa jeunesse. La ressemblance exacte compte moins que les caractères, les expressions et les attitudes familières. Son dessin fait revivre ce monde avec humour et tendresse. Sa Femme au ruban bleu provient de la collection Habib Boularès. Le peintre et l’écrivain ont également travaillé ensemble : Zoubeir Turki a conçu les décors et les costumes de sa pièce Mourad III . Cette provenance rappelle les liens entre les artistes, les écrivains et le théâtre dans la Tunisie indépendante. Reproduite en couverture de la revue syrienne Cinema Life au printemps-été 1989, cette œuvre à la gouache et au crayon sur papier sera présentée le 8 décembre, avec une estimation de 1 500 à 2 000 euros. De l’atelier de Roubtzoff à la collection d’Habib Boularès, ces portraits ont aussi une histoire de transmission. Leur passage chez Millon remet en circulation des œuvres qui racontent autant les choix des peintres que la place donnée à la peinture dans les familles et la vie culturelle tunisiennes. D’après le site de Millon . Les œuvres «tunisiennes» de Roubtzoff bientôt exposées à Cannes L’article De Roubtzoff à Zoubeir Turki, les Tunisiennes au premier plan est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Élections locales : 24 millions d’Algériens aux urnes, les enjeux du scrutin
items.description: Près de cinq mois après les élections législatives du mois de juillet dernier, un peu plus de 24 millions d’Algériens sont appelés, de nouveau, ce samedi, à élire leurs représentants au sein des Assemblées populaires communales (APC) et des Assemblées populaires de wilaya (APW). Au total, 162.864 candidats, dont 141.388 pour les APC et 21.476 pour les APW, briguent les suffrages des électeurs, à travers 6.065 listes, pour les 1.541 communes et les 69 wilayas que compte désormais le pays, selon les derniers chiffres de l’ANIE. Élections locales : un taux de participation plus élevé que les législatives ? Comme souvent en pareilles circonstances, les élections locales sont de nature à susciter une participation plus importante que les législatives, en raison notamment de la proximité qu’elles entretiennent avec les citoyens et des enjeux concrets liés à la gestion quotidienne de leur environnement. Routes, écoles, éclairage public, collecte des déchets, logement, transport, emploi ou encore aménagement urbain sont autant de préoccupations qui touchent directement à la vie des habitants. Durant toute la campagne électorale, qui s’est achevée mardi à minuit, les candidats et les états-majors des partis se sont ainsi employés à convaincre les électeurs de se rendre aux urnes, en privilégiant notamment le travail de proximité. Tous, ou presque, ont multiplié les sorties sur le terrain, les rencontres avec les citoyens et les meetings, dans l’espoir de rallier les suffrages. Bien entendu, les discours ont largement porté sur les questions de développement, l’amélioration des conditions socio-économiques, l’environnement, l’emploi, la culture et les préoccupations quotidiennes des habitants. En revanche, les questions politiques de fond sont restées relativement absentes des interventions. Rares sont les partis et les candidats qui se sont hasardés à aborder les grandes orientations politiques ou à engager un véritable débat sur les choix nationaux, encore moins à décliner leurs programmes concernant les grands dossiers. Quand l’intelligence artificielle s’invite dans la campagne Fait notable de cette campagne : les candidats et leurs soutiens ont largement investi les réseaux sociaux pour promouvoir leurs candidatures. Certains ont même eu recours à l’intelligence artificielle pour confectionner leurs affiches et leurs supports de communication. Mais cette nouvelle pratique n’a pas toujours produit les effets escomptés. Des visuels approximatifs, des erreurs dans les noms des candidats et des partis, des drapeaux ou des cartes déformés, ainsi que des portraits ne correspondant pas toujours à l’apparence réelle des postulants, ont parfois transformé ces opérations de communication en objets de moquerie. La campagne a également été ponctuée de scènes pour le moins insolites, dont les réseaux sociaux se sont emparés pour les tourner en dérision. C’est le cas, par exemple, de ces candidats du Front El Moustakbal dans une commune de la wilaya de Saïda, apparus vêtus de rose, suscitant des commentaires sarcastiques. À El Menia, l’image d’un garde du corps tenant une mallette noire a fait également les choux gras de la Toile, donnant lieu à un déluge de moqueries des internautes, tandis que des séquences du célèbre film « Carnaval fi dechra », campé par l’inimitable Athmane Ariouet, ont foisonné sur diverses plateformes pour parodier certaines scènes de la campagne électorale, notamment des candidats qui ont choisi les tambours et les chansons pour accompagner leurs tournées électorales. À ces scènes se sont ajoutées des séquences vidéo devenues virales, notamment celles de candidats s’exprimant en anglais devant des électeurs qui ne pratiquent pas nécessairement cette langue dans leur vie quotidienne. Une déclaration attribuée au président du Mouvement El Bina, Abdelkader Bengrina, a également suscité les sarcasmes. Selon les propos relayés sur les réseaux sociaux, Donald Trump aurait été impressionné par la campagne électorale algérienne et aurait envisagé de s’en inspirer pour les États-Unis. Autant de séquences qui ont contribué à donner à cette campagne une dimension parfois ubuesque, au détriment du débat de fond sur les programmes et les projets locaux. Une présence féminine plus visible et des meetings de proximité Au-delà de ces faits parfois burlesques, la campagne a aussi donné à voir une certaine évolution dans la perception de la compétition électorale et dans la manière dont les partis investissent le terrain. La présence des femmes dans l’animation des meetings et sur les affiches a été particulièrement remarquée, y compris dans des localités longtemps considérées comme fortement conservatrices. Autre élément qui mérite d’être relevé : on retrouve désormais des femmes portant le hijab (voile islamique) sur les listes de partis dits laïcs ou démocrates, tandis que des candidates sans voile figurent sur des listes de formations islamistes. Au niveau local, la compétition semble également dépasser, dans certaines circonscriptions, les clivages partisans traditionnels. C’est du moins ce qui a été donné à lire à travers certaines sorties de proximité et certaines réactions des présents. Vu sous cet angle, une partie des électeurs pourrait davantage s’intéresser au profil des candidats, à leur ancrage dans la commune et à leur capacité supposée à répondre aux préoccupations des habitants qu’à l’étiquette politique qu’ils portent à proprement parler. Il semble ainsi s’éloigner, du moins dans certaines localités, le temps où le choix électoral reposait essentiellement sur la sympathie ou l’attachement à un parti. Les enjeux pour les partis politiques Si le scrutin local est souvent présenté comme une échéance où la proximité avec les citoyens peut favoriser la participation, son enjeu dépasse largement la seule gestion des communes et des wilayas. Pour les formations politiques, il s’agit aussi de consolider leur implantation territoriale, de mesurer leur poids électoral et de retrouver une visibilité sur la scène politique. Les résultats leur permettront de jauger leur capacité de mobilisation et de disposer, ou non, de relais dans les assemblées élues. Reste que cette échéance intervient dans un contexte socioéconomique, pour le moins difficile, et par un passif de gestion controversé de nombre d'élus, ce qui pourrait influer sur le taux de participation. Elle est marquée également par l’entrée en vigueur de la nouvelle loi organique relative aux partis politiques. Le texte a notamment durci les conditions encadrant le fonctionnement des formations politiques. Une des dispositions prévoit notamment que le ministre chargé de l’Intérieur peut demander en justice la dissolution d’un parti qui ne présente pas de candidats à au moins deux échéances électorales consécutives. La participation aux scrutins constitue donc désormais un enjeu qui dépasse la simple recherche de sièges : elle engage aussi la pérennité institutionnelle des formations politiques. items.title: Gov’t plans Natural Resource Revenue Management Act to strengthen accountability – Deputy Minister
items.description: The government is proposing a Natural Resource Revenue Management Act to strengthen transparency, accountability and the long-term management of revenues generated from Ghana’s petroleum, minerals and other extractive resources. The Deputy Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Dr Yusif Sulemana, said the proposed legislation would establish a comprehensive framework for managing the country’s natural resource revenues and ensure they supported sustainable national development. Speaking on behalf of the sector Minister, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, at the 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards in Accra on Friday, November 27, Dr Sulemana said the government was committed to managing the country’s natural resource wealth in a manner that preserved opportunities for future generations. He said the country’s approach to mining and natural resource management must go beyond maximising immediate economic returns to securing long-term benefits. “Our task is not simply to maximise the benefits of mining today, but to also preserve and expand the opportunities that mining can create tomorrow,” he said. Dr Sulemana said the proposal was among several measures outlined in the government’s 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy aimed at strengthening the management of Ghana’s natural resource wealth. He explained that the proposed Natural Resource Revenue Management Act would provide a unified and more comprehensive framework for managing revenues from petroleum, minerals and other extractive resources. According to him, the initiative demonstrates the government’s determination to improve transparency and accountability in the utilisation of natural resource revenues while ensuring their long-term value to the country. He said effective management of extractive revenues was essential to ensuring that the benefits of Ghana’s natural resources were sustained and translated into meaningful development for present and future generations.

items.title: Deputy Minister urges Chamber of Mines to sustain role in Ghana’s development ahead of 2028 centenary
items.description: The Deputy Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Dr Yusif Sulemana, has urged the Ghana Chamber of Mines to build on its history of service and strengthen its contribution to the country’s development as it prepares to mark its centenary in 2028. He commended the Chamber for its constructive engagement with government, saying its criticisms, recommendations and policy contributions had helped shape reforms and regulations in the mining industry. Speaking on behalf of the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, at the 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards in Accra on Friday, November 27, Dr Sulemana encouraged the Chamber and its members to sustain their partnership with government to advance the sector. “As the Chamber approaches its centenary in 2028, I encourage you to build on your distinguished history of service, and continue strengthening your role as a constructive partner in Ghana’s development, especially in the mining industry,” he said. He acknowledged the Chamber’s contribution to policy discussions under the current administration, noting that its constructive criticisms and inputs had been valuable in shaping decisions affecting the sector. “Your constructive criticisms, your input has really helped us within these few years that this administration has had to do with some policies and regulations in the mining industry,” he added. Dr Sulemana’s remarks underscored the government’s recognition of the importance of sustained collaboration between the public and private sectors in developing Ghana’s mining industry. He urged the Chamber to maintain its constructive relationship with government as it approaches the historic milestone, while continuing to contribute to policies and initiatives that support responsible mining and national development.

items.title: US military says cyber systems secure after reports of Air Force hack
items.description: The US military denied Friday any issues with its computer security following media reports that the Air Force’s cloud-based system was hacked , in what would be the latest high-profile breach of US digital infrastructure in recent weeks. Asked whether the Air Force’s Cloud One platform had been hacked, the Pentagon did not specifically deny that the system had been breached. Instead, a Defence Department official told AFP late Friday that “The Department of War’s systems are safe, secure, and managed 24-7 by the best experts and teams in the world. We will continue to maintain all mission-critical operations and applications.” “As a matter of policy and operations security, the Department of War does not comment on the status of our networks,” a Defence Department official said earlier on Friday. NBC News, reported Friday citing an unnamed US official that the cloud platform had been breached and that an attack “could have exposed sensitive military information.” The breach was first reported by Reuters earlier Friday. Federal News Network , which specialises in covering US federal agencies, also confirmed the breach, citing a “person familiar with the incident.” The contractors discovered the hack earlier in the year while doing maintenance on the system, Federal News said. The reported attack is the latest in a string of major outages in US government and private-sector digital infrastructure. In recent weeks the CIA and FBI were also reportedly subject to hacks. Suppliers for major American financial institutions including JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard were also hit. In other instances, such as a major Microsoft Outlook outage , a separate US air traffic control issue and a reported issue with a top-secret National Security Agency (NSA) network earlier this month, officials were at pains to blame the outages on maintenance or defects – not intrusions. The attacks and outages are not limited to the United States. The European Commission last week said it came under an AI-assisted cyberattack in October. AFP was hit by a cyber attack on Thursday, forcing a major client-facing system to be taken offline.

items.title: Adenta police seize 125 motorbikes in crackdown on fake number plates
items.description: The Adenta Police District Command has seized 125 motorbikes in a security operation aimed at identifying riders using unregistered machines and motorcycles fitted with suspected counterfeit number plates. The exercise, carried out on Thursday, November 26, is part of a broader police effort to prevent the use of motorcycles in criminal activities and enforce compliance with road traffic regulations. District Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Samuel Lartey Lawson, said the seized motorcycles would undergo thorough checks to determine whether their registration documents and other statutory requirements were genuine. The checks will cover vehicle registration, insurance, riders’ licences and roadworthiness certificates. He said the operation was prompted, in part, by the use of unregistered motorcycles by criminals to carry out robberies, particularly in the early hours of the day. Chief Superintendent Lawson cited incidents in which market women were targeted by motorbike-riding assailants who made away with their cash and mobile phones. He warned that riders who could not produce the required documents would be processed for court, while those whose papers were found to be authentic would be allowed to retrieve their motorcycles. “Those who have genuine documents will be released,” he said.

items.title: Ghana Navy plans river bases to keep galamsey operators at bay
items.description: The Ghana Navy is preparing to establish military forward operating bases along major rivers nationwide as part of efforts to prevent illegal miners from reclaiming areas cleared during anti-galamsey operations. The proposed deployments are expected to provide a permanent security presence on vulnerable waterways, making it more difficult for illegal mining activities to resume after enforcement teams have withdrawn. The plan will be spearheaded by the Navy’s newly created Riverine Command, which has been tasked with coordinating security operations on inland water bodies, particularly rivers heavily affected by illegal mining and pollution. The Flag Officer Commanding the Western Naval Command and Second Garrison Commander, Commodore Stephen Billins Nyam, announced the initiative at the Second Garrison Media Soirée in Sekondi. He said the Navy had already identified major rivers across the country and selected strategic locations for the proposed bases, although the full deployment was still being rolled out. Commodore Nyam explained that the strategy was intended to address a major weakness in the fight against illegal mining: the return of operators to locations after security personnel have completed clearance exercises. He said the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) was undertaking targeted operations to drive illegal miners out of affected communities, but cautioned that such interventions would have limited impact if the areas were not subsequently secured. “Currently, NAIMOS is operating a surgical operation to get them out. But if you get them out and you don’t stay there to police it, the galamsey operators will come back,” he said. The Navy commander said the establishment of forward operating bases would ensure that security personnel remained on the waterways to consolidate the gains made through the operations. He stressed, however, that the deployment was still at an early stage, with the planning and establishment process under way. “These are all planned on paper. The establishment has started, but it is not complete,” he said, adding that the Navy intended to extend its presence to all major river bodies as the Riverine Command expanded its operations. Commodore Nyam also disclosed that the Navy intended to take charge of the Blue Water Guards it had trained, as part of a broader effort to strengthen protection of the country’s rivers. He said naval personnel were collaborating with NAIMOS and bringing their experience in maritime and riverine security operations to the fight against illegal mining.

items.title: Foire internationale de Lomé : Le ministre Badanam Patoki invite les exposants à renforcer la compétitivité de leurs entreprises
items.description: Lomé, 27 nov. (ATOP) – « J’invite l’ensemble des exposants à saisir pleinement l’opportunité qui est offerte pour promouvoir les produits et services, développer les réseaux, renforcer la compétitivité et conquérir de nouveaux marchés ». Cette invite a été faite par le ministre de l’Economie et de la Veille stratégique, Badanam Patoki lors de la cérémonie d’ouverture de la 21 ème édition de la Foire international de Lomé (FIL) le vendredi 27 novembre. Pendant dix-sept jours, cette foire fera découvrir le savoir-faire, la créativité et le dynamisme technologique de divers pays participants, en occurrence l’Inde, pays invité d’honneur. Pour le ministre, ce rendez-vous économique permettra au Togo de consolider sa position comme espace d’échanges, de commerce et d’investissement au service de son économie et de l’intégration régionale. « Dans un contexte où la compétitivité des économies repose de plus en plus sur la capacité à créer des connexions, à attirer les investissements, à développer les entreprises et à conquérir de nouveaux marchés, notre responsabilité collective est de faire de nos rendez-vous économiques de véritables espaces de création de valeurs », a indiqué le ministre. Cette édition, a-t-il poursuivi, doit également offrir aux investisseurs et aux entreprises internationales une meilleure visibilité sur les opportunités post-Togo et au-delà de l’espace économique de l’Afrique. « C’est pourquoi j’encourage les opérateurs économiques à faire de leur participation à cette édition une véritable démarche du développement commercial. La réussite de cette participation se mesurera par la qualité des contrats établis, les contrats envisagés et les opportunités créées ». Le ministre en charge de la Veille stratégique a salué le leadership et la vision du Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé qui a fait de ce cadre, un creuset des affaires non seulement pour les opérateurs économiques togolais, mais aussi pour ceux de la sous-région ouest-africaine et du reste du monde. Ce cadre commercial, a-t-il ajouté, facilite les contacts entre les entreprises, favorise la découverte de nouveaux produits et services et crée surtout les conditions nécessaires au développement de nouvelles relations commerciales et de nouveaux partenariats. Le ministre a aussi rappelé l’importance que le gouvernement accorde au développement du secteur privé, à la promotion de l’entrepreneuriat et au renforcement de la compétitivité des entreprises dans le pays. ATOP/DHK/AR

items.title: Fire ravages female hostel at St John Bosco’s College of Education
items.description: Several female students of St John Bosco’s College of Education in Navrongo are counting their losses after a fire swept through parts of their hostel, destroying personal belongings. The outbreak occurred while many of the students were away attending lectures, with preliminary reports indicating that no casualties had been recorded. Some students who noticed the fire reportedly made attempts to contain the flames before personnel of the Ghana National Fire Service arrived at the scene to bring the situation under control. Although the blaze affected sections of the female hostel, the full extent of the destruction was yet to be determined as assessments continued. The cause of the outbreak also remained unknown at the time of reporting. The incident has left affected students facing the loss of personal effects, with attention turning to the assessment of the damage and the support that may be required to help them recover. There were no immediate reports of injuries or loss of life.

items.title: La commune de Maluku se dote d’un plan local pour lutter contre l’insécurité
Les femmes du ministère du Développement local en guerre contre les cancers du sein et de la prostate
items.description: Agoè-Nyivé, 27 nov. (ATOP) – Le ministère délégué auprès du ministère de l’Aménagement du territoire chargé du Développement local, à travers sa cellule focale genre, a organisé un atelier de sensibilisation, d’information et de prévention de son personnel contre les cancers, le vendredi 27 novembre à Agoè-Nyivé. Cette sensibilisation est placée sous le thème, « Santé, prévention, et bien-être des femmes et des hommes au travail ». Elle s’inscrit dans le cadre de la campagne mondiale « Octobre Rose et Novembre Bleu » dédié à la sensibilisation et à la lutte contre le cancer du sein et de la prostate. L’initiative vient soutenir la volonté du ministère de garantir un environnement de travail sain et inclusif, où la santé et le bien-être des femmes et des hommes est considéré comme une priorité. Elle répond également aux engagements nationaux et internationaux en matière de droits humains, d’égalité de genre et de développement durable. La finalité est de contribuer à la promotion de la santé et du bien-être des femmes et des hommes au sein du ministère à travers la sensibilisation, la prévention et la mobilisation collective contre les cancers du sein et de la prostate. Par ailleurs, il s’agit pour la cellule genre de rendre compte de ses activités et de recueillir les recommandations du personnel pour l’amélioration de la performance du ministère. Les communications ont permis au personnel de renforcer les connaissances sur les facteurs de risque, les signes précoces et l’importance du dépistage du cancer du sein et du cancer de la prostate. La séance a aussi favorisé l’adoption de bonnes pratiques de santé au travail. D es professionnels de santé et experts en genre ont échangé avec le personnel du ministère sur le thème de la journée, suivi de recommandations adaptées au contexte dudit ministère. La présentation des différentes activités réalisées par la cellule genre a été faite, suivi de débats et échanges autour des difficultés, les bonnes pratiques ainsi que les solutions envisagées. Des recommandations et avis ont été recueillis pour les perspectives. La présidente de la cellule focale genre, Mme Pindra Samiya, représentant le ministre en charge du Développement local, a fait savoir que « pendant trop longtemps, la peur, la pudeur ou l’idée fausse que « cela n’arrive qu’aux autres » nous ont empêchés d’en parler. Pourtant, la vérité est simple : le silence protège la maladie, mais la parole protège la vie ». Elle a relevé qu’« en réunissant ces deux campagnes, nous refusons que le tabou gagne du terrain. Nous affirmons haut et fort que prendre soin de soi n’est pas un signe de faiblesse, mais un acte de courage et d’amour envers ceux qui nous entourent. Se faire dépister, poser des questions, écouter son corps : ce sont des gestes simples qui transforment la peur en pouvoir d’agir ». Mme Pindra a invité ses collègues à faire de ce moment bien plus qu’un simple débat, mais le point de départ d’une prise de conscience collective, qu’elles porteront bien au-delà des murs. Les activités de la cellule vont se poursuivre le mois prochain avec la présentation des rapports et les perspectives de l’année prochaine. ATOP/KYA/AJA

items.title: Evil or Helping Angel? How one librarian keeps AI honest and accurate
items.description: By Ebele Orakpo The widespread adoption of Artificial Intelligence has sparked growing concerns over its societal impact. Critics warn that heavy reliance on AI weakens critical thinking, creativity, and human mentorship in education while widening the digital divide. Also, creative industries face job displacement, copyright theft, and unauthorised likeness cloning. Digital markets are flooded with mass-produced AI content, devaluing human artistry. In this chat with Vanguard, Mr. Amed Demirhan, one of the pioneers of e-library worldwide and the General Manager/Director of the Barzani National Memorial Library and Museum in Kurdistan, Iraq, deviates from the norm of merely learning how to operate AI and advocates for training AI to maximize its output. The former Director of Library Services, American University of Nigeria, Yola, argues that this proactive approach can preserve jobs previously considered vulnerable to automation and concludes that human intelligence is still the ultimate. Excerpts: Training the AI Like many new innovations, AI sharply divides public opinion. While some praise it as an exceptional breakthrough, others view it as very dangerous, raising serious ethical concerns like information manipulation. However, I believe AI remains one of the most effective research assistants one can get. AI capabilities AI can perform complex tasks associated with human intelligence, including learning, adapting, analyzing information, problem- solving, and remembering. Within seconds, it can browse billions of global, multilingual records and resources—far exceeding the collections of the largest physical national libraries—to retrieve requested information. However, as a human creation, AI reflects all human imperfections. Just like any student, researcher, or research assistant, it requires proper training to become truly effective. Otherwise, when you ask a question or direct it to gather research information, it will retrieve overwhelming, unhelpful results, much like sailing across the vast ocean without a compass or clear direction. Set the rules Training AI with information literacy standards, including evaluating source content, verifying facts, checking author and publisher credibility, and citing properly, makes it far more effective for academic researchers. Beyond these foundational standards, we can add tailored, research-specific rules to target unique project needs. The AI operates strictly within a structured framework rather than searching randomly if instructed to retain these guidelines. My rules I rely on a strict set of principles when working with AI; I call these “my rules” because, much like students, AI does not always follow instructions automatically. Instead of constantly repeating my guidelines when requesting research, I simply tell it to follow “my rules.” Usually, it remembers the standards and corrects its output. While I did not invent these guidelines myself, as they are standard academic rules, I simplify my instructions to the AI by referring to them simply as “my rules.” Strict academic standards These are some of the rules I set for the AI:Research generated must be factual, precise, evidence-based, and academically defensible. *No fabrication. The AI is explicitly instructed never to invent facts, dates, quotations, citations, documents, or historical events. *Distinguish between hard evidence and human interpretation. Documented facts, estimates, scholarly opinions, and mere assumptions must never be treated as same. *Read the full context. Statements must always be read in their full context, evaluated against the weight of cumulative evidence rather than judged in isolation.Sources and verification •Prioritize primary sources using original archival documents, diplomatic correspondence, official records, and contemporary evidence whenever available. •Verify original documents by checking the actual source before attributing statements or quotations. •Cross-reference evidence by comparing historical findings with relevant independent sources. •Identify conflicting evidence and not to silently resolve contradictions or discrepancies between sources. •Respect source limitations by explicitly acknowledging when a document or claim could not be verified.Citations and References •Always use APA 7th edition rule book.•Provide accurate author names, publication dates, document titles, page numbers, and archival identifiers. •Include retrieval dates for online archival materials when appropriate. (It is not required but it is important to have.) •Never invent missing bibliographic information. Editorial work preservation of original text •Do not change my wording and anything in my text, just make recommendations. •When reviewing my writing, I recommend grammatical corrections in parallel sentence by sentence. Translation, transliterations, and transcribing •When translating, preserve the original meaning without adding interpretations and don’t change anything. •Mark illegible passages rather than guessing. •Transliterate precisely without adding or changing anything; mark any illegible letters clearly and never guess. *When transcribing historical documents, reproduce the original text faithfully and 100 per cent. Academic Evaluation •Keep evaluations short, factual, and strictly academic. (No stories and no theories) •Evaluate the argument actually presented rather than introducing unrelated criticisms. •Recognise the professional knowledge and firsthand research experience of a subject specialist. •Do not automatically require separate documentation for every statement grounded in the author’s professional experience. •Distinguish scholarly interpretation and strategic proposals from claims requiring empirical verification. Always remember my rules The AI will not always follow the rules but one has to remind it about the rules and verify information. Let me give some examples of how these rules work and what happens when they are not followed. One: ‘Keep evaluations short, factual, and strictly academic.’ Without this instruction, the AI will generate overly long responses that take too much time to read. Because this would happen after every request, it would waste valuable time. Therefore, this instruction is essential for making the AI more effective. Two: AI writing skills – Many teachers restrict or ban students from using AI in their writing. This is wrong, as it denies students access to a valuable learning tool. While AI can generate an essay or research paper in 20 to 30 seconds, the resulting work is often ineffective. Instead, teachers should instruct students on how to use AI responsibly to improve their own writing. For example, writers should prompt the AI with a strict rule: “Do not change my wording or anything in my text; only provide recommendations.” This allows the author to preserve their original voice while receiving actionable feedback on how to improve. The same rule applies to grammar correction, where the AI must be restricted to suggesting edits rather than rewriting entire sentences. Used this way, AI functions much like a writing tutor in a university writing lab. Three: Ethical use of resources – An important element of ethical use is proper citations. If you don’t tell an AI which citation style to use, it will pick one at random and give you a different format every time. That is why one of my main research rules is to instruct it to always use APA 7th edition. Even though it isn’t always required for online sources, I also tell it to add the retrieval date right before the link. It doesn’t always follow this perfectly, but it gets it right most of the time—and when it forgets, I just remind it of “my rules.” Even as technology advances and changes, our fundamental ethical values remain the same. Humanity has upheld principles like righteousness, integrity, morality, honesty, and respect for thousands of years. In fact, what universities teach today about the ethical use of research resources is much the same as it has always been. Conclusion AI is an exceptionally great research assistant with multiple abilities. Nevertheless, it has to be focused and regulated for more effective research. A strong human supervision is still required for evaluations and verifications. The ultimate responsibility for research rests with human beings, not AI. Vanguard News The post Evil or Helping Angel? How one librarian keeps AI honest and accurate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: God will not take sides in an election – Nana Akomea
items.description: New Patriotic Party (NPP) Third Vice-Chairman, Nana Akomea, has challenged attempts to attribute electoral victories and defeats to spiritual intervention, insisting that election results are determined by voters rather than divine preference. He said political parties and their supporters should not interpret electoral outcomes as evidence that God had favoured one side over another, dismissing suggestions that the NPP’s defeat in the 2024 general election had a spiritual dimension. Speaking in an interview on Citi FM on Friday, November 27, Mr Akomea maintained that elections were human contests in which competing political parties sought the support of the electorate. “There’s nothing spiritual about an election. God will not take sides in an election,” he said. He explained that although supporters of different political parties were entitled to pray for electoral success, such prayers should not be confused with divine intervention in the outcome of a democratic contest. To illustrate his argument, Mr Akomea drew a comparison with a football match between Accra Hearts of Oak and Asante Kotoko, noting that supporters of both clubs could pray for their respective teams to win, but only one could emerge victorious. He cautioned against bringing God into political and other human disagreements, arguing that divine authority should not be associated with the competing interests of political actors. “We shouldn’t put God in the arena of human conflict. He’s above that,” he stated. Mr Akomea also took issue with suggestions that spiritual forces could influence large numbers of voters to abandon their preferred political choices at the polls. He questioned how millions of Ghanaians who voted for the NPP and the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in previous elections could have been collectively influenced by spiritual forces to determine the outcome. He maintained that the results of elections should instead be understood as an expression of the choices made by voters. His comments come amid discussions within the NPP over the factors behind the party’s defeat in the 2024 general election, including its losses in constituencies traditionally regarded as its strongholds. Mr Akomea’s position is that the party must view electoral outcomes as the product of voters’ decisions rather than seek spiritual explanations for its performance at the polls.

items.title: Death toll in Baloch Colony building collapse rises to 11 as rescuers recover three more bodies
items.description: KARACHI: Rescue workers recovered three more bodies from the rubble of a six-storey building that collapsed near Karachi’s Baloch Colony area on Saturday, taking the death toll to 11. On Wednesday, three people were killed and 14 others injured when the under-construction building — reportedly being constructed illegally on a residential plot — collapsed . Another body was recovered on Thursday, taking the death toll to four . On Friday, four more bodies were recovered, taking the toll to eight . Videos shared by Rescue 1122 from the site showed members of the Urban Search and Rescue team using heavy-duty bolt cutters to cut through rebar and recover bodies, while clearing rubble with various tools. At least eight more people are still missing, according to reports submitted by their relatives at the information desk set up at the site of the collapsed building. Commissioner’s office submits report to CM The Karachi Commissioner’s Office has submitted a report to the chief minister on action taken against illegal and unauthorised buildings in the city, stating that 516 buildings have been sealed so far as part of an ongoing crackdown, as of November 27. According to the report, action was taken against 262 buildings under construction in various districts. Of these, 158 were sealed, while notices were issued to 12 buildings. Construction work was found to have been halted at one site during an inspection. In Korangi district, 41 of the 48 buildings were sealed, while notices were issued to seven. In Keamari, 12 of the 19 buildings were sealed and notices were issued to five, while construction work was found to have stopped at one site. The report also recorded 12 buildings in West, 21 in Malir, 64 in Central, 61 in South and 37 in East. Of these, eight buildings in Malir, five in Central, 55 in South and all 37 in East were sealed. Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi has directed deputy commissioners to continue action against illegal and unauthorised constructions and ensure that those violating building regulations are dealt with in accordance with the law. Man rescued alive after 54 hours A day earlier, emergency services rescued a man alive from beneath the rubble, two days after the building collapsed. Rescue 1122 said that 28-year-old Muhammad Adil was rescued alive from the rubble. It said that the search operation for any other individuals feared trapped was underway. Its spokesperson, Hassaanul Haseeb Khan, termed the rescue a “breakthrough”. He added that rescue operations were ongoing to search for other survivors from the debris. He said the rescued man told them that two other persons who might be alive were in touch with him. However, Khan said the rescuers conducted a search in the identified area but could not locate them. Khan added that heavy machinery was also being used to remove debris, but that whenever a human body was spotted in the debris, the team stopped the machine operations and initiated manual work with extra care to recover the body. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah expressed gratitude that the man trapped under the rubble survived for 54 hours, describing it as a “miracle”, according to a statement issued from his office. According to the statement, the chief minister directed rescue agencies and the Karachi commissioner to accelerate the ongoing rescue operation and deploy all available resources. Murad also praised rescue workers for their tireless efforts and directed officials to ensure the survivor receives the best possible medical treatment. Sindh Local Government Secretary Waseem Shamshad, who also served as director general of the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA), was removed from both posts on Thursday on the directives of CM Murad following the incident. The CM ordered sweeping action over the incident while chairing a high-level meeting, further issuing directives for the removal of East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi, as well as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East Zubair Sheikh, over “negligence”, a statement issued by the CM Office said. In addition to the removal of the three officials, CM Murad further issued directives for the suspension of 16 SBCA officials and the initiation of an inquiry against them. He directed the police to “immediately” arrest the building’s owner, Salman Tahir, and the builder, Zeeshan. Moreover, he instructed that the building’s architect and structural engineer be included in the incident’s investigation to determine whether the construction complied with approved plans, building regulations and safety standards. 14 ‘illegal’ buildings in KAEHS to be demolished The KDA’s Additional Deputy DG Farhan Kaiser visited the site on Thursday and told the media that their first priority was to remove the debris. He said that under the directions of the Sindh CM and LG minister, “illegal buildings” were being sealed across the metropolis. He said that so far, 14 buildings had been sealed in the KAEHS after the building collapse and would be demolished in a second phase of the operation. Kaiser added that it was the responsibility of the residents to report illegal buildings in their respective areas, and vowed to take action against the builders and owners of these buildings. Members of the Chief Minister Inspection Team (CMIT), Bilal Memon and Anwar Shar, visited the scene and collected samples of the material used in the construction of the building for investigation purposes. Rehabilitation secretary Rafiq Mustafa Shaikh, SBCA DG Abid Saleem, Rescue 1122 DG Brig. (retd) Wajid Sibghatullah Mahar and Rescue 1122 COO Dr Abid Jalaluddin Shaikh also visited the site and supervised the rescue operation. FIR registered A first information report (FIR) of the incident was registered at the Tipu Sultan police station on Wednesday, on the complaint of an official of the Sindh Local Government Department. The FIR, seen by Dawn , invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder), 119 (public servant concealing design to commit offence), 427 (mischief causing damage), 337-H(1) (hurt caused by rash or negligent act), 109 (abetment) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code. The building’s four owners — including Salman Tahir whose arrest the Sindh CM has ordered — its builder, architect, structural engineer and its contractors have been nominated in the FIR. According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that poor-quality material was being used in the construction of the building. He claimed that the suspects, in collusion with the officials of various government departments, had been involved in constructing additional structures and not complying with the building’s approved plan. This was why the building collapsed around 1pm, the complainant alleged. Police have arrested four of the suspects, including one of the owners, Saad Tahir, and three contractors, who were produced before the judicial magistrate (south) today. The judge granted police a five-day physical remand of the suspects.

items.description: Two journalists from the Multimedia Group Limited have been recognised at the 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards held in Accra on Friday, November 27. Nana Boakye Danquah Yiadom emerged winner of the Best Mining Reporter category, while Caleb Wuninti Ziblim was named second runner-up. The recognition celebrates their contributions to mining journalism and efforts to promote public understanding of developments in Ghana’s mining industry. Nana Boakye Danquah Yiadom clinched the top award ahead of Timothy Ngnenbe of Graphic Communications Group Limited, who was named first runner-up, and his Multimedia Group colleague Caleb Wuninti Ziblim, who placed third. The awards form part of efforts by the Ghana Chamber of Mines to recognise excellence in reporting on the mining sector and acknowledge the role of journalists in promoting transparency, accountability and informed public discourse.

items.title: Mahama targets single Africa-Caribbean market under Ghana’s AU chairmanship
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has outlined an ambitious plan to deepen economic and diplomatic relations between Africa and the Caribbean, with the integration of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) into a common market among his priorities for Ghana’s African Union (AU) chairmanship in 2027. He said Ghana would also work towards making the African diaspora’s recognition as the AU’s Sixth Region a practical reality, giving people of African descent a stronger role in the continent’s development and decision-making processes. Addressing a joint sitting of the Parliament of Barbados in Bridgetown on Friday, November 27, during his state visit, President Mahama said the historical connections between Africa and the Caribbean should provide the foundation for a more coordinated economic and diplomatic partnership. He identified four priority areas for cooperation: trade integration, renewable energy and the blue economy, development of the creative industries, and academic collaboration. On trade, the President said the two regions had significant opportunities to expand commercial relations by bringing their respective economic arrangements closer together. He pointed to the AfCFTA Secretariat in Accra, which coordinates the continent’s 54-member free trade initiative, covering more than 1.4 billion people and a combined economic output exceeding US$3.5 trillion. President Mahama said the scale of the African market presented considerable opportunities for Caribbean businesses, adding that his government would engage regional leaders to explore arrangements for extending the benefits of the continental trade agreement to CARICOM countries. Addressing Barbados Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley, he pledged to work with leaders of the region to establish mechanisms for expanding AfCFTA to cover Caribbean countries. He said the initiative would open up new opportunities for trade, investment and business partnerships while strengthening the economic relationship between the two regions. The President also proposed closer collaboration in renewable energy and the sustainable use of marine resources, describing Barbados as an important example in the transition towards cleaner energy. He called on universities, engineers and private businesses in Africa and the Caribbean to explore joint ventures in solar energy, sustainable fisheries and ocean conservation. He said cooperation in the green and blue economies could transform the Atlantic Ocean, which historically separated the two regions, into a platform for shared economic opportunities and sustainable development. On the creative economy, President Mahama identified music, film, fashion and the arts as important areas through which Africa and the Caribbean could deepen their cultural connections while creating economic opportunities for young people. He drew attention to the rich musical traditions of both regions, citing Ghana’s Highlife, Hiplife and Afrobeats alongside Barbados’ Soca, Spouge and Bashment. However, he expressed concern that ownership of intellectual property, digital streaming platforms and the royalties generated from creative works often remained outside the regions where the content was produced. To address the challenge, he proposed harmonising intellectual property regulations, establishing joint investment funds for young creatives and developing financial technology and artificial intelligence platforms owned and controlled by innovators from the two regions. He said stronger collaboration would enable African and Caribbean creatives to retain greater economic value from their work and compete more effectively in the global entertainment industry. The fourth area of cooperation focused on education and research, with the President advocating stronger institutional partnerships between universities in Ghana and Barbados. He proposed closer collaboration between the University of the West Indies’ Cave Hill campus and Ghanaian institutions, including the University of Cape Coast, the University of Ghana and the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology. He further called for structured student exchange programmes that would allow young people from both countries to experience each other’s educational systems and cultures. Under the proposal, students would have the opportunity to spend at least one semester studying in Ghana and another in Barbados. The initiative, he said, would help nurture a new generation of Africans and Caribbean people with a deeper understanding of their shared history and greater capacity to pursue common development goals. The university exchange proposal builds on an earlier call by President Mahama for school exchange arrangements involving institutions in Cape Coast and Barbados during his engagements in Speightstown. His parliamentary address also followed a series of announcements concerning closer bilateral relations, including proposed visa waivers, direct air connections and opportunities for Ghanaian nurses to work in Barbados. President Mahama, who was the second Ghanaian Head of State to address the Barbadian Parliament, said the future of Africa-Caribbean relations must move beyond historical and cultural connections to embrace practical economic cooperation. He said Ghana’s anticipated leadership of the AU in 2027 would provide an opportunity to advance that vision and strengthen the role of the African diaspora in the continent’s development.

items.title: Pakistan Railways man booked for transporting dogs in train’s power van in Lahore
items.description: LAHORE: During checking at Raiwind Railway Station, the railway police’ special branch staff recovered on Friday two dogs being transported illegally, without booking, in the Allama Iqbal Express (9-Up) power van. According to officials, the train’s power plant operator, Mohammad Khan, allegedly charged Rs5,000 for transporting the dogs from Karachi, without booking them under the prescribed railway procedure. The animals were reportedly to be handed over to a person at Kot Lakhpat Railway Station. The police initiated legal proceedings against the operator, registering a case against him for violating railway regulations. The dogs were subsequently booked, and a fine of Rs7,690 was deposited into the railway’s account, officials said. Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

items.title: Mahama sings Peter Tosh’s ‘African’ in Barbados Parliament
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama brought a touch of reggae and Pan-African history to the Parliament of Barbados when he broke into lines from Jamaican reggae icon Peter Tosh’s 1977 song, African , during an address highlighting the ancestral ties between Ghana and the Caribbean nation. The president used the musical interlude to reinforce his message that geographical boundaries and nationalities could not erase the common heritage of Africans and people of African descent. Addressing a joint sitting of the Barbadian Parliament on Friday, November 27, 2026, during his state visit, President Mahama drew on Tosh’s celebrated song to make the case for a stronger sense of identity and solidarity among people of African descent. Quoting from the song, he reminded his audience of its central message: that African identity transcends nationality and geographical origin. “We are all Africans,” he declared, adding that genuine brotherhood required the courage to continue seeking justice for their ancestors. The moment provided a cultural highlight to an address that traced the historical connections between Ghana and Barbados to the transatlantic slave trade and the forced displacement of millions of Africans. President Mahama said the Atlantic Ocean, which had historically separated Africans from their ancestral homes, should now serve as a bridge for renewed relationships, cooperation and shared prosperity. He pointed to cultural similarities between the two countries, including language, food, music, communal savings traditions and respect for elders, as evidence of their enduring connections. He cited the similarities between Ghanaian staples such as kenkey and banku and Barbados’ cou-cou, as well as the presence of the Akan-derived susu savings tradition in Caribbean society. The President also paid tribute to Africans who endured enslavement and whose labour contributed to the wealth of Europe and North America. He argued that the historical injustice remained an unfinished matter, particularly because enslaved Africans received no compensation when slavery was abolished, while slave owners were compensated by imperial governments. On reparatory justice, he said the pursuit was not intended to promote retribution but to secure historical recognition, accountability, reconciliation and the restoration of human dignity. He referenced the adoption of a United Nations General Assembly resolution on the trafficking and enslavement of Africans, describing it as an important step in the continuing campaign for reparatory justice. The President also called for greater practical cooperation between Ghana and Barbados, including stronger trade relations, direct air links, educational exchanges and closer economic integration between Africa and the Caribbean. He said Ghana was committed to making the African Diaspora’s designation as the African Union’s Sixth Region operational when the country assumes the AU chairmanship in 2027. Mr Mahama’s address was delivered as Barbados marked 60 years of independence and five years as a republic. He congratulated the country on the milestones and praised its development and governance record. He was the second Ghanaian President to address the Barbadian Parliament, an occasion he described as a reflection of the longstanding friendship between the two countries.

items.title: L’Algérie lance « Mawadda » pour faire face au fléau du divorce
items.description: Avec plus de 90.000 divorces enregistrés chaque année, soit plus de 240 séparations quotidiennes, et une forte baisse des mariages, l’Algérie fait face à une progression préoccupante des ruptures conjugales. Un constat qui place la préservation de la cellule familiale au cœur des préoccupations et auquel les pouvoirs publics entendent répondre à travers un nouveau programme national baptisé « Mawadda », axé sur la prévention et l’accompagnement des futurs couples. Un dispositif axé sur la prévention familiale La ministre de la Solidarité nationale, de la Famille et de la Condition de la femme, Soraya Mouloudji, a présidé, mardi 24 novembre, à l’École nationale d’administration, le lancement du programme national d’accompagnement familial « Mawadda », ainsi que de la première session nationale de formation des formateurs dans ce domaine. Cette initiative vise à renforcer les mécanismes de conseil et d’accompagnement familial, prévenir les conflits conjugaux et promouvoir le dialogue au sein des foyers. La ministre a souligné le rôle central de la famille dans la transmission des valeurs et la cohésion de la société, insistant sur la nécessité de mieux préparer les couples à leurs responsabilités conjugales et éducatives. La ministre a indiqué que ce programme vise à « renforcer et développer les compétences spécialisées des cadres du secteur dans les domaines du conseil familial, de la préparation à la vie conjugale et des approches préventives modernes », ainsi qu’à « mettre en place un réseau national spécialisé de formateurs qualifiés, répondant à des normes unifiées et rigoureuses ». Des formations déployées dans les wilayas dès 2027 D'une durée de deux mois, la première session de formation s'adresse aux cadres des Directions de l’action sociale et de la solidarité (DASS). Elle combine enseignement présentiel et à distance autour de six axes. Dès 2027, les cadres formés assureront, au niveau local, des sessions destinées aux jeunes souhaitant se marier et fonder une famille. L'objectif est de leur transmettre les connaissances psychologiques, sociales et juridiques nécessaires à une vie conjugale équilibrée. Un programme lié à la protection des femmes Le lancement de « Mawadda » coïncide avec la Journée internationale pour l’élimination de la violence à l’égard des femmes, célébrée le 25 novembre sous le slogan « La dignité de la femme est celle de la société ». Une rencontre scientifique réunissant des spécialistes des domaines religieux, juridique, social et médical a également été organisée autour du rôle de la préparation au mariage dans le renforcement de la cohésion familiale. À cette occasion, la ministre a rappelé que la préservation de la famille algérienne constitue une responsabilité collective nécessitant l'implication de l'ensemble des institutions et des acteurs de la société. L’article L’Algérie lance « Mawadda » pour faire face au fléau du divorce est apparu en premier sur TSA .
